title: Opinion: AMD’s Lisa Su takes center stage at CES, taking aim at Intel and Nvidia
Opinion: AMD’s Lisa Su takes center stage at CES, taking aim at Intel and Nvidia
summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su used her CES keynote to confidently declare that the company expects to challenge and potentially surpass bigger rivals like Intel and Nvidia. She detailed AMD’s 2019 plans for computers, servers, and videogames, featuring new high-end graphics cards and a second-generation server chip. Su showcased the performance of early versions of AMD's 7-nanometer hardware against offerings from its competitors.

title: Ambarella's CV25 camera SoC with CVflow computer vision processing | Security News
summary: Ambarella has unveiled the CV25 camera System-on-Chip (SoC), part of its CVflow family, designed for next-generation intelligent solutions. This SoC integrates advanced image processing, high-resolution video encoding, and CVflow computer vision processing into a low-power design. The CV25 enables AI at the edge for applications like home monitoring, surveillance, and automotive solutions, supporting features such as facial recognition and driver monitoring.

title: NVIDIA Resets The Self-Driving Bar Again With AutoPilot Supporting 'Level 2+'
summary: NVIDIA announced its DRIVE AutoPilot system at CES 2019, which it describes as the "world's first commercially available Level 2+ automated driving system" that will enable supervised self-driving vehicles by 2020. The company also revealed that Mercedes-Benz has chosen NVIDIA as its AI partner for developing next-generation vehicles. Additionally, NVIDIA launched the new GeForce RTX 2060 GPU and announced over 40 new gaming laptops featuring GeForce RTX GPUs.

title: Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC review: "A beautiful machine with performance to match"
summary: This article reviews the Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC, highlighting its powerful components, excellent dual-chamber design, and brilliant RGB lighting. While acknowledging its large size and non-overclockable CPU, the review praises its performance at 1080p and 1440p and its overall value for gamers seeking a pre-built machine.

title: Amazon Stock Rises as the 'Scout' Delivery Robot Is Unveiled
summary: Amazon announced the launch of its new delivery robot, "Scout," a cooler-sized ground unit designed for autonomous package delivery, initially accompanied by an Amazon employee. This announcement led to a 0.91 percent rise in Amazon's stock prices. The article also mentions other strong performers in the Entrepreneur Index™, including NVIDIA Corp. and Analog Devices, while J.M. Smucker Company, OReilly Auto Parts, and Brown-Forman Corp saw declines.

title: Caterpillar, Nvidia Warnings Send Wall Street Tumbling
summary: U.S. stocks tumbled following warnings from Caterpillar and Nvidia, which highlighted concerns about a slowing Chinese economy and the impact of tariffs on corporate profits. Caterpillar missed profit estimates due to softening demand in China and rising costs, while Nvidia cut its revenue forecast due to weak demand and lower data center sales. This sent major indexes like the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite lower, despite overall positive earnings reports.

title: China weakness spreads far and wide, from Caterpillar to Nvidia
summary: Major US and European companies like Caterpillar, Nvidia, and Intel are reporting significant impacts from the slowing demand in China across various sectors, from industrial machinery and technology to automotive parts. While many industries are feeling the pinch, luxury goods and some consumer brands like Tiffany & Co. and Starbucks are, for now, experiencing continued growth, creating a mixed economic picture. The emerging trend suggests a broadening slowdown in China is affecting a diverse range of goods and services.

title: Will Top-Down Hardware/Software Co-Design Ever Happen?
summary: This article discusses the long-standing challenge and evolution of hardware/software co-design in the EDA industry over the past two decades. Author Frank Schirrmeister reflects on past predictions and notes the significant progress made in verification, virtual prototyping, and the "shift left" methodology, even if not exactly as anticipated. He concludes that new abstraction layers and tools, like those for iOS and Android, and middleware like OpenGL, are enabling a new level of hardware/software optimization.

title: Opinion: AMD has won Wall Street’s trust, and its stock is showing the results
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) has gained significant credibility on Wall Street, a trust it previously lacked. Despite reporting slightly below-expectation fourth-quarter revenue and a first-quarter outlook due to excess graphics chip inventories, the stock did not face a typical decline. This indicates Wall Street's growing faith in CEO Lisa Su's ability to deliver, especially with a forecast heavily weighted to the second half of the year.

title: NVIDIA Responds to TRC Capital’s ‘Mini-Tender’ Offer
summary: NVIDIA has issued a response to an unsolicited "mini-tender" offer from TRC Capital Corporation to purchase up to 1,000,000 shares of NVIDIA's common stock at $149.88 per share. NVIDIA is not affiliated with TRC, expresses no opinion on the offer, and advises shareholders to consult with their brokers or financial advisors and exercise caution. The company also clarified that a mini-tender offer is an offer for less than 5 percent of a company’s shares and is not subject to the same disclosure requirements as larger tender offers.

title: Aehr launches FOX-CP wafer-level test & reliability screening system
summary: Aehr Test Systems has launched the FOX-CP, a new low-cost single-wafer test and reliability verification system designed for logic, memory, and photonic devices. This system, part of the FOX-P product family, is optimized for shorter test times, multiple touchdowns, and includes features like 2048 Universal Channels, making it suitable for silicon photonics and VCSEL arrays. The FOX-CP helps reduce test costs by identifying failing die before packaging and is available for order and shipment.

title: SoftBank Sells Entire Nvidia Stake
summary: SoftBank's nearly $100 billion Vision Fund sold its entire 4.9% stake in Nvidia Corp. in January, realizing a $3.3 billion return. This move comes as Nvidia's shares have been affected by trade war fears and projected lower-than-expected revenue, leading to a nearly 50% loss in value since October 2018.

title: Make Your Data Pipeline Super-Efficient by Unifying Machine Learning and Deep Learning
summary: This article discusses how NetApp and NVIDIA technologies can unify and accelerate data pipelines for machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL). It highlights the inefficiencies of traditional approaches that separate data preparation, ML, and DL stages, and proposes a combined solution using NVIDIA RAPIDS and NetApp's Data Fabric and ONTAP AI to create a seamless, end-to-end AI pipeline from edge to core to cloud. The integration aims to reduce data sprawl, improve processing efficiency, and solve specific data science challenges with features like FabricPool, FlexCache, and FlexClone.

title: Coke stock heads for worst day since 2008, Nvidia looks to capitalize on ‘positive set up’
summary: Coca-Cola Co. (Coke) stock is experiencing a significant downturn, heading for its worst day since 2008, largely due to "softness" in its North America business, a revenue miss, and a disappointing outlook for the year. The company is facing challenges in regions like Argentina and Turkey and plans to increase marketing expenses in 2019, despite some encouraging trends in North America and China. The article also mentions Nvidia looking to capitalize on a positive setup, alongside other earnings watch updates for Six Flags, Avon, and Yeti.

title: Machine learning is the biggest disruptive tech: AMD CTO Mark Papermaster
summary: AMD CTO Mark Papermaster discusses the significance of the company's new 7nm chips in meeting the insatiable demand for computational power, especially in data centers and mobile devices. He highlights machine learning as the biggest disruptive technology, noting its potential to leverage data and predict results, while also addressing concerns about AI and robotics replacing human jobs. Papermaster also touches on GPU usage in the crypto space, indicating AMD's focus on broader GPU markets in gaming, servers, and blockchain.

title: Nvidia to Acquire Mellanox, Its Biggest Deal Ever at Roughly $7 Billion
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire networking firm Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for approximately $6.9 billion, marking its largest acquisition to date. This move is aimed at strengthening Nvidia's position in cloud computing, following a downturn in its core graphics-chips business. The deal signifies Nvidia's continued expansion beyond its traditional graphics processing unit market into new technology areas.

title: NVIDIA to pay $6.9 billion for Israeli company Mellanox
summary: NVIDIA is set to acquire Israeli company Mellanox for $6.9 billion. This acquisition highlights a significant investment in Israeli technology and business, as ISRAEL21c is now part of the Unpacked family, focusing on smart, engaging, and inspiring content about Israel, Judaism, and the Jewish experience.

title: Nvidia acquires Mellanox against growing AI, data competition
summary: Nvidia has acquired Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing and competitive market for AI and data-intensive computing platforms. This merger aims to bolster their combined capabilities against new rivals like Amazon and Cray, as both companies already have a significant presence in high-performance computing (HPC) with their integrated technologies. The acquisition is seen as a strategic move to address increasing competitive challenges in the HPC market.

title: Nvidia to make largest acquisition in its history with $6.9 billion deal for Mellanox
US gaming firm Nvidia to buy Israeli chip maker Mellanox for $6.9 billion
summary: US gaming and computer graphics giant Nvidia Corp. is set to acquire Israeli chip maker Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion in cash. This deal marks the second-largest tech acquisition in Israel's history and will enhance Nvidia's capabilities in high-speed data center solutions. Mellanox, founded in 1999, specializes in servers and storage switching solutions and has seen significant demand for its products.

title: Nvidia to buy Mellanox for $6.9 billion as it pushes into data centers
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire chipmaker Mellanox Technologies Ltd. for $6.9 billion, a move aimed at bolstering its presence in the expanding data center market. The acquisition is Nvidia's largest ever and seeks to accelerate its successful initiatives in providing graphics chips for artificial intelligence work in data centers. The deal signals a potential resumption of consolidation within the semiconductor industry, despite concerns about regulatory approvals amid the U.S.-China trade war.

title: ‘Happy and sad day,’ Mellanox founder says of $6.9 billion sale to Nvidia
summary: Mellanox Technologies founder and CEO Eyal Waldman expressed mixed feelings about Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of his company, calling it a "happy and sad day." The deal, Israel’s second-largest tech acquisition, will see Nvidia acquire Mellanox for $125 a share, aiming to strengthen its position in the data center components market. Waldman, who founded Mellanox in 1999, indicated that while the sale was the right move for shareholders and employees, his own future at the firm remains undecided.

title: Nearly Half of Israel's Largest Exporters Are Foreign-Owned
summary: Nearly half of Israel's 20 largest exporters, each with over $1 billion in annual sales, are foreign-owned, according to Calcalist data. Five are U.S.-owned, two European-owned, and one each by Chinese and Mexican companies. This trend was underscored by Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of Israeli chipmaker Mellanox Technologies Ltd.

title: Global Computer Companies Announce NVIDIA-Powered Enterprise Servers Optimized for Data Science
summary: Seven major systems manufacturers, including Cisco, Dell EMC, and HPE, are now offering NVIDIA T4 servers optimized for data science. These NVIDIA NGC-Ready validated servers feature T4 GPUs and CUDA-X AI acceleration libraries, providing a highly efficient platform for data analytics, machine learning, and deep learning. NVIDIA also launched an enterprise support service for NGC-Ready systems and announced T4 server certifications for virtual desktop and application virtualization solutions.

title: NVIDIA’s Isaac SDK brings modern AI to autonomous machines
summary: NVIDIA announced the public availability of its Isaac SDK, a free robotics developer toolbox designed to accelerate innovation and deployment of AI in autonomous machines. The SDK provides Isaac applications, GEMs (robot capabilities), a Robot Engine, and Sim, aiming to simplify the integration of AI for perception, navigation, and manipulation. The platform supports various NVIDIA Jetson platforms, including the new low-cost Jetson Nano, and offers open-source hardware reference designs.

title: Postmates Presents New NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier Equipped Delivery Robot at GTC
summary: Postmates unveiled Serve, an all-electric autonomous delivery robot equipped with NVIDIA's Jetson AGX Xavier module, at GTC Silicon Valley. The robot can carry 50 pounds over 30 miles and is designed to efficiently move items over short distances in cities. Serve uses Velodyne LIDAR sensors and NVIDIA's technology, with Postmates aiming for zero-cost deliveries to consumers.

title: Mellanox to stay independent within Nvidia with Waldman at its head, CEO says
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced that Mellanox Technologies Ltd., following its $6.9 billion acquisition by Nvidia, will operate as an independent unit and retain all employees, with plans to grow the workforce in Israel. Mellanox founder and CEO Eyal Waldman will continue to lead the unit. This acquisition marks Nvidia's largest to date, aimed at expanding its reach into data centers crucial for AI and machine learning.

title: Nvidia CEO: Every Big Company Wants To Be In Israel Today
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated during a visit to Israel that every major company desires a presence in the country, highlighting strong foreign investment in its high-tech sector. His visit followed Nvidia's $6.9 billion acquisition of Israeli company Mellanox Technologies, a move that will make Israel Nvidia's second-largest employee base. Nvidia plans to continue investing in Israel's technology talent and excellence, recognizing the country as a crucial global tech hub.

title: NVIDIA Is A Data Center Company Now
summary: NVIDIA's acquisition of Mellanox for $6.9 billion signifies its strategic shift from primarily a GPU company to a full-fledged data center company. This move leverages NVIDIA's success in High-Performance Compute (HPC) and AI with GPUs, integrating Mellanox's data center networking expertise to address the growing demands of data science and hyperscale workloads. The article highlights how NVIDIA is expanding its ecosystem to support diverse data center needs, from specialized accelerators to broader infrastructure solutions.

title: Ushering in a new wave of video surveillance capabilities
summary: Next-generation IP cameras, powered by advanced AI-enabled chips, are revolutionizing video surveillance by processing data at the edge, offering real-time analytics for professional and consumer markets. This on-device processing enhances privacy, reduces network and storage costs, and enables faster reaction times for critical events. The technology is set to impact retail, smart cities, and home monitoring by providing valuable insights and improved security.

title: Qualcomm Announces New AI Chip for Cloud Data Center Servers
summary: Qualcomm Inc., a leader in smartphone technology, is entering the crowded market for AI chips used in cloud data centers. The company plans to leverage its mobile expertise and advanced manufacturing to deliver power-efficient products, aiming for a share of a market projected to reach $17 billion by 2025. This move positions Qualcomm to compete with established players like Intel, Nvidia, and cloud providers already developing AI components.

title: Qualcomm aims to take on Nvidia, Intel with new AI chips
summary: Qualcomm is entering the artificial intelligence chip market with its new Cloud AI 100 chip, aiming to compete with Nvidia and Intel. The company plans to target smaller, simpler data centers with power-efficient chips designed for "inference" tasks, leveraging its expertise from mobile phone chip development. Testing with partners like Microsoft is expected to begin later this year, with mass production in 2020.

title: Xpeng Motors debuts at Auto Shanghai 2019, premiering the Xpeng P7 intelligent electric coupe
summary: Xpeng Motors unveiled its new production model, the P7 intelligent electric coupe, at Auto Shanghai 2019. The P7 boasts a 4s-to-100km/h acceleration, 600 km+ NEDC range, and a Level 3-ready autonomous driving platform. It combines NVIDIA DRIVE Xavier and Qualcomm Snapdragon 820A processors, and features Xpeng's XPILOT 3.0 autonomous driving system tailored for China's road conditions.

title: Intel roadmaps leak showing company's plans through 2021 - CPU - News
summary: Purported Intel mobile and desktop processor roadmaps have leaked, reportedly from a Dell presentation, detailing plans through Q4 2021. The roadmaps show the introduction of Comet Lake H series processors (14nm) and Ice Lake U (10nm) for mobile, and similar 14nm Comet Lake H and speculative 10nm Rocket Lake processors for desktops, indicating a slower transition to 10nm than previously anticipated by some.

title: AMD's 50th Anniversary Reminds Us Why The Company Matters
summary: This article reflects on AMD's 50th anniversary, highlighting its resilience, innovation, and historical milestones under various leaders, currently Lisa Su. The author, a long-time observer of AMD, discusses the company's evolution from its founding in 1969 to its current focus on high-performance computing, emphasizing its commitment to execution and a people-centric culture. The piece celebrates AMD's ability to consistently bounce back from challenges and its vision for future technological innovation.

title: Investors Sue to Block Mellanox-Nvidia Deal, Report Says
summary: A shareholder of Mellanox Technologies Ltd. has filed a class-action lawsuit to block the company's acquisition by Nvidia Corp. for $6.9 billion. The suit alleges that Mellanox failed to provide sufficient information to the SEC regarding Nvidia's bid and criticized JP Morgan's analysis of the deal. The transaction, announced in March, is expected to be completed later this year.

title: Using HashiCorp Nomad to Schedule GPU Workloads | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: HashiCorp Nomad 0.9 introduces device plugins, including one for NVIDIA GPUs, allowing Nomad clients to detect, fingerprint, and make hardware devices available for scheduling workloads. This feature enables users to specify GPU requirements like count, memory, and model type in job specifications, optimizing task placement for GPU-accelerated applications. The article demonstrates how this integration supports deep learning inference applications using NVIDIA's TensorRT Inference Server on a GPU-enabled Nomad cluster.

title: Release! CORSAIR ONE i140/i160, small size of 12L
summary: Lynx International Inc. has launched the CORSAIR ONE i140 and CORSAIR ONE i160 compact gaming desktop PCs in Japan. These computers feature a small 12L body while packing high-spec components like Intel Core processors and NVIDIA GeForce RTX GPUs, alongside advanced cooling solutions for stable operation. The CORSAIR ONE i140 is priced at 399,800 JPY and the i160 at 479,800 JPY, both released on May 11, 2019.

title: Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:ESGV)
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF (ESGV), including its current price, key statistics, fund overview, expenses, and recent news headlines. It highlights ESGV's investment strategy, which focuses on U.S. all-cap companies screened for environmental, social, and corporate governance criteria, and lists its top holdings and sector exposure. The fund, managed by Vanguard, has assets under management of $11.58 billion and a net expense ratio of 0.09%.

title: India's leading gaming company receives NVIDIA Certification
summary: CIRCLE Gaming, an Indian gaming peripherals manufacturer and cafe operator, has received NVIDIA certification. This recognition highlights CIRCLE Gaming's growth and business acumen, expanding from one cafe to over thirty in three years. NVIDIA views this as a step towards creating a world-class gaming ecosystem in India, recognizing CIRCLE Gaming's success in integrating product and industry expertise in the cafe business.

title: With Cray Deal, HPE Finally Enters The HPC Big Leagues
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is acquiring supercomputer maker Cray for $1.3 billion, net of Cray's cash, strategically positioning HPE in the high-performance computing (HPC) sector. This acquisition allows HPE to leverage Cray's exascale system wins and Slingshot interconnect technology, while providing Cray with the financial heft and market reach of a larger company. The deal is expected to solidify HPE's competitive standing against rivals like Dell and IBM in the HPC market.

title: DEEP FOCUS: Understanding Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock
summary: This article provides a deep dive into Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock, analyzing its market position, competition, product segments, financial trends, and cash flow situation. It highlights AMD's stock performance, its rivalry with Intel, and the anticipated impact of new product launches on its future growth and market share amidst the US-China trade war concerns.

title: ‘Quake II RTX,’ NVIDIA’s Reimagining of PC Gaming Classic with Ray-Traced Graphics, Available Now
summary: NVIDIA announced the release of 'Quake II RTX,' a fully path-traced version of the classic PC game, available now as a free download on Steam and nvidia.com. This title is the world's first game to be fully path-traced, unifying all lighting effects into a single ray-tracing algorithm. The release includes the first three single-player levels, with the full game, including multiplayer, available for existing Quake II owners with the RTX upgrade.

title: Invesco S&P 500 GARP ETF
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Invesco S&P 500 GARP ETF (SPGP), which targets growth stocks within the S&P 500 exhibiting quality characteristics and attractive valuations. It outlines the ETF's methodology, performance metrics, expenses, top holdings like NVIDIA and Uber, and compares it against peers in terms of concentration, valuation, and dividends. The fund is positioned for investors seeking growth stocks without overvalued companies, acknowledging its fees are higher than some ultra-low-cost alternatives.

title: Nvidia responds to AMD with ‘Super’ gaming cards
summary: Nvidia has launched a new "Super" brand line of its RTX Turing-based gaming cards in response to rival Advanced Micro Devices Inc. The new cards, which allow real-time ray tracing, include the RTX 2060 Super, RTX 2070 Super, and RTX 2080 Super, with release dates scheduled throughout July. An analyst suggests Nvidia's marketing of these chips will be crucial in fending off AMD's challenge.

title: Rekor joins Nvidia’s Metropolis Software Partner Program
summary: Rekor Systems Inc has joined the Nvidia Metropolis Software Partner Program, using Nvidia GPUs to accelerate its OpenALPR vehicle recognition software. The Metropolis platform leverages AI for smarter cities, enabling Rekor's software to accurately scan and recognize license plates, vehicle details, and support applications like law enforcement and traffic management. This collaboration enhances OpenALPR's speed, accuracy, and scalability, reducing hardware costs for customers.

title: IOTA DLT integrated with major manufacturer STMicroelectronics
summary: The IOTA Foundation announced a partnership with STMicroelectronics to integrate its DLT (directed acyclic graph or tangle) technology with ST's electronic devices, enabling immediate access to the tangle for users of ST components. This collaboration aims to advance IoT technology by providing a scalable and fee-free blockchain solution for connected smart devices. STMicroelectronics, with a market cap of $15.8 billion, is a major electronics firm producing sensors and semiconductors for a vast global client base.

title: KeyShot 9 to support GPU rendering through Nvidia RTX ray tracing and AI denoising
summary: Luxion has announced that KeyShot 9, set for release in Autumn, will incorporate Nvidia RTX ray tracing and AI denoising for GPU rendering. This marks a significant shift as KeyShot has traditionally relied on CPU-based ray tracing, but Luxion emphasizes that users will have seamless control and choice between CPU and GPU rendering workflows. Supported graphics cards include Nvidia GeForce, Quadro, and Tesla products with Maxwell and newer generation GPUs.

title: Nvidia jumps on earnings beat
summary: Nvidia's stock rose after reporting better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter earnings, beating analyst estimates for both revenue and earnings per share. Despite an annualized revenue decline of 17%, driven by decreases in gaming and data center segments, the company offered optimistic guidance for the third quarter's gross margin. Analysts noted a potential return to normalcy in the second half of 2019, citing strong market positioning for Nvidia's GPUs.

title: HP Announces CEO Is Suddenly Stepping Down, Stock Plunges Amid Mixed Earnings
summary: HP Inc. announced that CEO Dion Weisler is stepping down due to a family health issue, leading to a stock plunge despite mixed Q3 earnings that beat EPS but missed slightly on revenue. Enrique Lores, a long-time HP veteran, will succeed Weisler, who was instrumental in the company's cybersecurity focus. The change comes as HP aims to strengthen its position in the competitive PC market.

title: 5G Technology Making Its Way Into Self-Driving Cars
summary: 5G technology, specifically C-V2X, is set to revolutionize self-driving cars by enabling vehicles to communicate wirelessly for improved functionality and safety. Investors can capitalize on this emerging trend through ETFs like the iShares Self-Driving EV and Tech ETF (IDRV), which provides exposure to companies involved in self-driving and electric vehicle innovation. The article highlights the disruptive potential of 5G in various industries beyond just autonomous driving.

title: NVIDIA Quadro RTX 6000 Powers World’s Fastest Laptop — ASUS ProArt StudioBook One
summary: NVIDIA announced that the Quadro RTX 6000 GPU will power the ASUS ProArt StudioBook One, hailed as the world's most powerful laptop. This new system joins 11 other RTX Studio systems, bringing the total to 39, and is designed for creative professionals needing high-end workstation performance on the go. The laptop features 24GB of GPU memory, real-time ray tracing, and advanced thermal cooling, supporting demanding workflows like 3D animation, 8K video editing, and VR.

title: Taking a Look Under the Hood of VanEck’s Video Gaming and Esports ETF
summary: This article provides an in-depth look at the holdings within VanEck's Video Gaming and Esports ETF (ESPO), highlighting key companies from both Asia-Pacific and the U.S. It discusses the performance and business models of leading firms like Sea Limited, Bandai Namco, Square Enix, Advanced Micro Devices, Zynga, and Activision Blizzard. The article suggests that investing in a diversified ETF can offer targeted exposure to the high-growth video gaming and esports sector.

title: Nvidia’s TensorRT deep learning inference platform breaks new ground in conversational AI
summary: Nvidia has released a new version of its TensorRT deep learning inference platform, significantly improving performance for conversational AI. TensorRT 6 reduces inference times for BERT-Large to 5.8 milliseconds, making it practical for enterprise deployment. The platform also includes optimizations for speech recognition, 3D image segmentation, and industrial automation applications, while also enhancing support for dynamic input batch sizes.

title: Pure Storage Goes Wide On Flash: Intros Optane-Based Modules For Performance, QLC For Capacity
summary: Pure Storage expanded its all-flash storage array line with two key innovations: DirectMemory Modules for high-performance applications using Intel Optane and QLC-based FlashArray//C for capacity-optimized, more economical all-flash storage. These introductions aim to broaden Pure Storage's market reach by addressing both extreme performance needs and the demand for cost-effective, high-capacity flash solutions, making the all-flash data center more economically viable. The new offerings are designed to provide significant performance boosts and consolidate large-scale tier-two data, respectively.

title: You might have never heard of America's top-paying company
summary: Palo Alto Networks, a cybersecurity company, has been identified as America's highest-paying company in Glassdoor's latest ranking, offering a median total pay of nearly $171,000 annually. This figure surpasses well-known tech giants like Facebook, Google, and Microsoft. The company's focus on a growing industry—cybersecurity and cloud services—contributes to its high demand for talent and generous compensation.

title: The highest-paying company in 2019 pays a median salary of $170,929 — here are 9 other companies that pay the most
summary: Glassdoor compiled a list of the 25 highest-paying companies in 2019, with a focus on the top 10. These companies, primarily in tech, consulting, and finance, offer median employee salaries of $148,000 or above. Palo Alto Networks leads the list with a median staff salary of $170,929.

title: Avantis U.S. Equity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:AVUS)
summary: The Avantis U.S. Equity ETF (AVUS) is an exchange-traded fund that tracks the Russell 3000 index, launched on September 24, 2019, and managed by American Century Investments. It features a diversified portfolio of US equities with a bias towards smaller, more profitable, or value companies. As of January 9, 2026, AVUS was trading at $115.05, with $10.80 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.15%.

title: Apple says Mac Pro manufacturing will remain in Austin
summary: Apple announced on Monday that it will continue manufacturing its Mac Pro computers in Austin, Texas, reversing earlier reports of a potential move to China. This decision comes after the company secured tariff exemptions from the U.S. government for key imported parts, allowing it to avoid additional costs. Apple (AAPL) emphasized its commitment to U.S. manufacturing and its significant investment in the American economy, including its operations and planned expansion in Austin.

title: Semiconductor stocks are poised to benefit as industry sales growth resumes in 2020
summary: Semiconductor stocks are expected to see a rebound in sales growth in 2020, following a "reset" year in 2019. Despite volatility, these stocks have historically been strong long-term investments. The industry, significantly impacted by U.S.-China trade tensions, anticipates a return to growth with companies like Nvidia projected to see a 17% sales increase next year.

title: Inception Spotlight: Subtle Medical’s AI-based Medical Imaging Software Receives FDA Clearance
summary: Subtle Medical, an NVIDIA Inception member, secured FDA clearance for its AI-based SubtleMR imaging processing software. This technology uses deep learning to denoise medical images from existing MRI scanners, integrating into radiology workflows to improve patient experience and operational efficiency. The software leverages NVIDIA's hardware and software, including DGX Station, DGX-1, and T4s, achieving significant speedups with TensorRT.

title: NVIDIA with Microsoft Announces Technology Collaboration for Era of Intelligent Edge
summary: NVIDIA and Microsoft have announced a technology collaboration focused on intelligent edge computing to help industries manage and gain insights from vast amounts of data. This partnership integrates Microsoft Azure with the NVIDIA EGX platform and NVIDIA T4 GPUs to accelerate AI capabilities from the edge to the cloud. The collaboration aims to enable breakthrough experiences for customers across various industries, including retail, manufacturing, and smart cities.

summary: NVIDIA has launched its next generation of SHIELD TV, starting at $149, comprising two new models: SHIELD TV and SHIELD TV Pro. These devices feature the new Tegra X1+ processor, delivering 25% more performance, and support Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos for enhanced visual and audio experiences. The new SHIELD models also utilize AI upscaling for HD content to 4K resolution and offer access to a wide range of streaming, gaming, and AI capabilities.

title: Microsoft tops list of the most ‘just’ US corporations
summary: Microsoft Corp. has topped the list of America's Most JUST Companies for the second consecutive year, recognized for its commitment to workers, communities, and the environment. This milestone was achieved on Wednesday, July 8, 2020, with Nvidia's market cap reaching $251.31 billion compared to Intel's $248.16 billion. While other companies like Texas Instruments and Qualcomm have previously and temporarily held the top spot over Intel, this marks a significant achievement for Nvidia.

title: The 10 Biggest Networking Company Acquisitions Of 2020 (So Far)
summary: This article details the 10 biggest networking company acquisitions of 2020 to date, highlighting significant deals made by tech giants like Nvidia, Cisco, and F5 Networks. It covers purchases ranging from billion-dollar agreements to more strategic acquisitions aimed at expanding portfolios in areas like 5G, cloud security, and software-defined networking, despite the economic downturn caused by the global pandemic. The acquisitions underscore the dynamic nature of the networking market and companies' efforts to enhance their services and product offerings.

title: Nvidia market value closes in on Intel
summary: Nvidia is nearing Intel in market capitalization for the first time, fueled by a 70% stock surge this year due to the accelerated shift to cloud-based digital services. Nvidia's market cap has reached approximately $245 billion, just shy of Intel's $249 billion. This milestone would position Nvidia as the third-largest chipmaker globally by market cap, trailing only Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and Samsung Electronics Co.

title: NVIDIA Now Most Valuable US Chipmaker, Intel Falls Behind
summary: NVIDIA has overtaken Intel to become the most valuable U.S. chipmaker, with its market capitalization reaching $251.3 billion compared to Intel's $248.2 billion. This surge is attributed to NVIDIA's strong financial performance, its dominance in gaming and data center markets, rapid adoption of its GPUs in AI, efficient cost management, and robust cash flow. The company's stock has shown exceptional growth, rallying 73.7% year-to-date and over twenty-fold in the last five years.

title: Switzerland’s Logitech partners with India’s Gamer, Streamer Shagufta ‘Xyaa’ Iqbal
summary: Logitech, a Swiss and American computer peripheral manufacturer, has partnered with Indian gamer and streamer Shagufta Iqbal, known as Xyaa. This partnership comes as gaming companies increase online promotions. Xyaa, who has garnered over 200,000 YouTube subscribers and 80,000 Instagram followers, has a long-standing career in competitive gaming and previously worked as a Software Developer.

title: SoftBank Explores Sale or IPO for Chip Designer Arm Holdings
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is reportedly exploring options for its British chip designer Arm Holdings, including a full or partial sale or a public offering. The Japanese conglomerate acquired Arm four years ago for $32 billion. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is advising on the early-stage review.

title: Gartner’s 2020 Magic Quadrant for Data Center and Cloud Networking: Key Takeaways
summary: Gartner's 2020 Magic Quadrant for Data Center and Cloud Networking identifies 11 vendors, categorizing them into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players based on their vision and execution. Cisco, Arista Networks, and Juniper Networks were named Leaders, recognized for their investments in analytics, product portfolios, and automation capabilities. The report also highlights the strengths and market positions of Challengers like Huawei, Visionaries including VMware and Dell EMC, and Niche Players such as NVIDIA-Mellanox Technologies.

title: Lenovo Legion™ Offers More Ways to Raise Your Game
summary: Lenovo has expanded its Legion gaming PC lineup, integrating AMD Ryzen mobile and desktop processors into five new models. This expansion provides gamers with more choices and aims to deliver immersive experiences with improved performance, graphics, and display technology. The new offerings include Lenovo Legion laptops (17-inch Legion 5, Legion 5P, IdeaPad Gaming 3) and desktops (Legion Tower 5, IdeaCentre Gaming 5), all featuring advanced thermal solutions and high refresh rate displays.

title: New in July 2020: Playback Improvements for H.264 and HEVC on Windows
summary: Adobe has released updates for Premiere Pro and After Effects, significantly improving H.264 and HEVC playback performance on Windows Intel systems, offering up to a 2X speed increase due to collaboration with Intel. The update also introduces ProRes 4444 XQ export for macOS, previously Windows-only, and features the Roto Brush 2 in After Effects Beta, which uses Adobe Sensei for faster rotoscoping. These enhancements are part of Adobe's ongoing efforts to boost application quality and performance through strategic partnerships.

title: University of Florida and Nvidia partner to build academia’s fastest supercomputer yet
summary: The University of Florida and Nvidia Corp. are partnering to build what they claim will be the fastest artificial intelligence supercomputer in academia. This machine, an upgrade to UF's existing HiPerGator, will tackle issues like COVID-19 research, rising seas, and personalized medicine, and is made possible by a $25 million donation from Nvidia founder Chris Malachowsky and an additional $25 million in hardware and services from Nvidia. UF also plans to invest $20 million and aims to become a leading AI university, producing 30,000 "AI-enabled graduates" by 2030.

title: Intel's 7nm is Broken, Company Announces Delay Until 2022, 2023
summary: Intel announced a significant delay in the rollout of its 7nm CPUs, pushing their debut to late 2022 or early 2023. This delay is attributed to a "defect mode" causing yield degradation, putting Intel approximately twelve months behind its internal targets for 7nm process. The company is now exploring contingency plans, including the use of third-party foundries for some components and entire chip designs, and plans to increase shipments of 10nm chips by 20%.

title: Banking on AI: RBC Builds a DGX-Powered Private Cloud
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) has built an NVIDIA DGX-powered private cloud to enhance its AI capabilities and transform client experiences, leveraging a strategic investment in AI through its research institute, Borealis AI. This new infrastructure allows RBC to run thousands of simulations and analyze millions of data points rapidly, enabling the development of smart applications and significant savings in total cost of ownership. The initiative showcases RBC's commitment to innovation and its early adoption of emerging technologies to maintain its competitive edge in the financial services industry.

title: Nvidia sets 16 new performance records in latest MLPerf AI benchmarks
summary: Nvidia's latest A100 GPU and its DGX SuperPOD system achieved 16 new performance records in the third annual MLPerf benchmark tests, showcasing significant advancements in AI training. The company's hardware excelled in new recommendation systems tests, Natural Language Processing, and reinforcement learning. This performance highlights a four-times improvement over Nvidia's previous DGX system, reinforcing its position in the AI hardware market alongside other strong contenders like Google.

title: Arista, Juniper, Nvidia Switch Vendor ‘Leaders,’ Says Forrester
summary: A Forrester Research report on programmable switch vendors names Arista Networks, Huawei, Juniper Networks, and Nvidia as "leaders." Arista particularly stood out due to its flexible EOS operating system, while Cisco, despite its significant market presence, was placed in the "strong performers" and "contenders" categories for its IOS-XE and NX-OS platforms, respectively. Nvidia also had a dual presence, with its Cumulus Networks operations named a leader and its Mellanox acquisition a contender.

title: Hermann Hauser: ARM sale to Nvidia would be a disaster
summary: Hermann Hauser, co-founder of ARM, stated that a potential sale of the British chip designer to US firm Nvidia would be "disastrous." He argues that Nvidia, being a competitor to many of ARM's licensees, would compromise ARM's crucial neutrality, leading current licensees to seek alternatives. Hauser believes the UK government should intervene to help ARM become an independent British company once again, possibly through a public listing.

title: CHT, partners kick off self-driving bus services
summary: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT), Kingwaytek Technology, and Tamsui Bus have launched autonomous passenger transport services in New Taipei. The service utilizes an autonomous driving platform integrating C-V2X communication, self-driving buses built by Kingwaytek, roadside sensors, and a cloud monitoring system. CHT has also established a monitoring center to manage real-time data for smart transportation applications.

title: Fleet Dreams Are Made of These: TuSimple and Navistar to Build Autonomous Trucks Powered by NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: TuSimple and Navistar are partnering to build dedicated self-driving semi-trucks, with production slated to begin in 2024. These autonomous trucks will be powered by the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX platform, moving beyond retrofitted vehicles to custom-built designs optimized for self-driving systems. This collaboration signifies a major step towards widespread deployment of autonomous freight, supported by Navistar's infrastructure and TuSimple's HD map network.

title: How RBC Built Its Own GPU Farm for an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Banking Platform
summary: The Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), working with Red Hat and Nvidia, has developed an AI computing platform powered by a custom-built Nvidia GPU farm to enhance its banking services. This platform allows for extremely fast processing of client records and real-time analysis of market data, significantly improving efficiency compared to CPU-based systems. The collaborative effort not only benefits RBC but is also expected to provide valuable insights and technologies for the broader fintech industry and other sectors, as the partners gained considerable expertise in AI and cloud technologies.

title: Startup Lunit Uses AI to Help Doctors Prioritize Patients with COVID-19 Symptoms
summary: Lunit, a South Korean medical imaging startup, has developed an AI-based system called Lunit INSIGHT CXR to quickly detect pneumonia and other radiological findings on chest X-rays. This system is crucial for triaging COVID-19 patients by providing near-instant evaluations. The company has partnered with GE Healthcare and utilizes NVIDIA technology to commercialize its AI solutions, aiming to enhance medical diagnosis and treatment efficiency.

title: Atomwise Raises $123 Million to Accelerate AI Drug Discovery
summary: Atomwise, a drug discovery startup, has successfully raised $123 million, bringing its total capital to nearly $175 million. The funding will be used to scale its AI platform, develop its internal drug pipeline, and expand partnerships with companies like Eli Lilly and Bayer. Atomwise's AtomNet model utilizes a convolutional neural network to rapidly screen billions of compounds, significantly accelerating the small molecule drug discovery process with the help of NVIDIA GPUs.

title: Blaize Takes On Nvidia, Intel With Xplorer Edge AI Chips
summary: Blaize, an AI chip startup, is launching its Xplorer Accelerator cards and Pathfinder P1600 embedded modules to compete with Intel and Nvidia. These new products are based on a Graph Streaming Processors architecture that reportedly offers up to 60 times better system-level efficiency for edge AI applications compared to traditional CPU and GPU solutions. Blaize plans to target the market through OEMs, system integrators, VARs, and ISVs, leveraging its proprietary AI software suite.

title: The geopolitical implications of the microchip race
summary: The semiconductor industry has become a critical geopolitical battleground between the United States and China. Both nations recognize that winning the microchip race will confer a significant advantage in the ongoing great power competition. While China's domestic microchip production lags behind Western technology, the country could potentially close the gap by leveraging political power and securing foreign expertise, though U.S. efforts are aimed at thwarting these advancements.

title: Nvidia Expands Partner Program With New Incentives, Training
summary: Nvidia has enhanced its Partner Network with new incentives, industry-specific training, and improved sales tracking for its growing channel of over 1,500 members. Key additions include a fixed back-end rebate for Elite partners, dedicated market development funds, and an expanded "AI Champions Club." The company is also planning future expansions, such as integrating Mellanox and Cumulus Networks' partner programs and introducing a cloud service provider program.

title: NVIDIA to Host Digital GTC in October Featuring Keynote from CEO Jensen Huang and Continuous Programming Around the World
summary: NVIDIA announced its digital GPU Technology Conference (GTC) will run from October 5-9, 2020, featuring a keynote by CEO Jensen Huang and over 500 sessions. The conference will cover AI, data science, graphics, and more, with programming streams across multiple global regions. GTC will offer live demos, interactive sessions with experts, training workshops, and a startup track.

title: Swing Trading Semiconductors The IBD Way
summary: This article details Investor's Business Daily's (IBD) swing trading strategy for semiconductor stocks, emphasizing a shift from a semiconductor ETF to individual sector leaders like AMD and Nvidia. It highlights how the strategy adapted to the coronavirus market rally, initially gaining broad exposure through an ETF and later refining positions to focus on outperforming individual stocks. The piece explains IBD's method of identifying and investing in strong leaders for optimal swing trading results.

title: SoftBank builds $1.2 billion Amazon stake; invests in Netflix, Tesla
summary: SoftBank Group Corp has built a $1.2 billion stake in Amazon and also invested in Netflix, Tesla, Microsoft, and Alphabet, marking a strategic shift towards liquid stocks. This move comes as the company expands its investment activities beyond unlisted startups and its Vision Fund, which has recently seen its holdings fall below acquisition prices. The group is leveraging a massive asset sale program to buy shares in these tech giants, whose values are currently rising amidst a tech stock rally.

title: Nvidia hurdles $300 billion market cap, which Intel hasn’t topped since the dot-com bust
summary: Nvidia Corp. has surpassed a $300 billion market capitalization for the first time, establishing itself as the largest U.S. chip company. This milestone comes as Nvidia's stock has risen over 100% this year, while Intel's has declined by nearly 20%. Nvidia is set to report its second-quarter earnings soon after achieving this record valuation.

title: Gold Diggers; Nvidia ARMed; TSLA’s Chinese Bevy; Sorry Chevy
summary: This article discusses the current market trends in gold, Nvidia, Tesla, and General Motors. It highlights gold's rallying price despite being considered a "boring" investment, Nvidia's potential acquisition of ARM Holdings, Tesla's fluctuating registration numbers in China despite a rising stock price, and General Motors' reluctance to fully embrace the EV market. The article also provides a rundown of upcoming earnings reports in the retail and semiconductor sectors.

title: August NVIDIA Studio Driver Now Ready for Download — Brings Support for Adobe Premiere Rush, Premiere Pro and More Creative App Updates
summary: NVIDIA has released its August Studio Driver, which offers support for new updates across a range of creative applications including Adobe Premiere Rush, Premiere Pro, Blender, V-Ray 5 for Maya, Flicker Free, and BorisFX Optics. Key features include AI-powered tools in Adobe apps like Auto Reframe and Scene Edit Detection, OptiX acceleration for all NVIDIA GPUs in Blender, and performance enhancements in V-Ray 5 and Flicker Free. The update aims to improve productivity for creators, especially those working remotely, with increased speed and new functionalities.

title: Intel's next-gen Xe-HPG gaming GPU will be made by TSMC on 6nm in 2021
summary: Intel's forthcoming Xe-HPG gaming-focused graphics card, expected in 2021, will be manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) using their 6nm process node. This move positions Intel to compete directly with AMD and NVIDIA, as the Xe-HPG is rumored to include hardware ray tracing and GDDR6 memory. While Intel's Xe-LP and Xe-HP designs will be produced in-house on their 10nm SuperFin process, the strategic decision to utilize TSMC's 6nm node for the gaming GPU aims to provide a competitive edge against 7nm and 8nm offerings from rivals.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Our Future Is About ‘Data Center-Scale Computing’
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasized that the company's future hinges on "data center-scale computing" rather than just chip-level optimization. This strategy is highlighted by the recent acquisition of Mellanox and the success of its data center division, which for the first time surpassed gaming revenue. Huang stressed that innovation must encompass communication between chips and system-level solutions, including the DGX deep learning systems, to achieve holistic data center performance.

title: Nvidia earnings beat expectations, its data center business is bigger than its gaming business for the first time ever
summary: Nvidia reported better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter earnings, with overall revenue up 50% year-over-year. For the first time, its data center business, driven by AI workloads and the Mellanox acquisition, surpassed its gaming unit in revenue. CEO Jensen Huang anticipates a strong second half for gaming, despite declines in professional visualization and automotive segments due to the pandemic.

title: Nvidia Posts Record Sales as Pandemic Sustains Demand for Gaming, Data-Center Chips
summary: Nvidia reported record sales for its latest quarter, driven by strong demand for online gaming and remote computing services during the pandemic. The company's earnings per share also increased, exceeding Wall Street's expectations. Nvidia's stock has performed exceptionally well during the health crisis, making it the best-performing stock in the S&P 500.

title: Intel plans big stock buyback after shares plummet, boosting prices in after-hours trading
summary: Intel announced a plan to buy back $10 billion of its stock by the end of the year, following a nearly 19% drop in its shares over the past month. This decision resulted in a nearly 4% gain in after-hours trading. The company views these repurchases as prudent given that its shares are trading below intrinsic valuation, amidst struggles with new chip engineering and increased competition from rivals like AMD and Nvidia.

title: Apple worth $1 trillion more since COVID-19 crashed the NASDAQ 100
summary: This article highlights how certain tech companies, particularly Apple and Tesla, have seen significant market value increases since the NASDAQ 100's low point in March 2020 following the COVID-19 crash. Apple's market capitalization grew by over $1 trillion to surpass $2 trillion, while Tesla also experienced a remarkable recovery. The article also notes other companies like Mercadolibre, PayPal, NVIDIA, eBay, Align Technology, and Lululemon that showed strong rebounds, contrasting these with a couple of pharma stocks that had not fully recovered.

title: Reliance Industries Successfully Became The Second Largest Brand In The World After Apple In 2020
summary: Reliance Industries, led by Mukesh Ambani, was ranked the second-largest brand globally after Apple in the FutureBrand Index 2020. The company was recognized for its ethical behavior, growth, innovative products, and excellent customer service due to its transformation into an advanced conglomerate catering to diverse consumer needs, spanning petrochemicals, telecommunications, and more. FutureBrand highlighted that Reliance's success is partly due to its expansion and investments from Google and Facebook, positioning it for potential future growth in the rankings.

title: Pixel Perfect: V7 Labs Automates Image Annotation for Deep Learning Models
summary: V7 Labs, a U.K. startup, has developed an AI-powered web platform called V7 Darwin that automates image annotation for deep learning models. This platform is trained to detect and label almost any object, accelerating the training process by up to 50x compared to human annotation. V7 Darwin is optimized on NVIDIA GPUs and is being applied across various industries, including healthcare, manufacturing, and agriculture, to improve efficiency and reduce costs associated with AI model development.

title: City's technology chief Louis Stewart hired away by Nvidia Corp.
summary: Louis Stewart, Sacramento's chief innovation officer, is leaving his municipal role to join Nvidia Corp., a Santa Clara-based technology company. He is expected to start his new position in mid-September.

title: Nvidia says its new 28B-transistor flagship graphics chip is fastest ever built
summary: Nvidia has launched its new RTX 30 series, a flagship line of consumer graphics cards. The top-tier RTX 3090 features 28 billion transistors and is considered the "fastest GPU ever built for gaming and creative types," capable of running 8K resolution games at 60 frames per second. This series, based on Nvidia's Ampere architecture, promises a significant generational leap in performance and power efficiency.

title: NVIDIA Delivers Greatest-Ever Generational Leap with GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled its GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs, powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivering the most significant generational performance leap in GeForce history with up to 2x the performance and 1.9x the power efficiency of the previous generation. These new GPUs, including the RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070, offer unprecedented real-time ray tracing and AI gaming capabilities, along with new tools like NVIDIA Reflex, Omniverse Machinima, and Broadcast. Fortnite is also integrating RTX real-time ray tracing, enhancing the gaming experience with advanced graphical features.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is the Most Important Company in the World
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) is highlighted as the world's most important company due to its dominant lead in advanced chip manufacturing technology, particularly in 7nm and 5nm processes. Despite its strategic importance and lead over competitors like Intel and Samsung, the stock's valuation is influenced by geopolitical risks related to its location in Taiwan and the ongoing tensions between the U.S. and China. The company is, however, exploring building a plant in Arizona to mitigate some of these risks.

title: Micron Announces GDDR6X Memory, Powering the World's Fastest Graphics Cards
summary: Micron Technology announced GDDR6X, the world's fastest discrete graphics memory solution, capable of reaching system bandwidths up to 1 terabyte per second. This new memory, developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, powers the new NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 and GeForce RTX 3080 GPUs, enabling advanced gaming experiences with high resolutions and real-time ray tracing. GDDR6X achieves its speed through innovative four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) signaling, significantly increasing memory bandwidth and offering lower power consumption per transaction.

title: ‘Fortnite’ Is RTX On! Real-Time Ray Tracing Comes to One of Most Popular Games on the Planet
summary: NVIDIA and Epic Games announced that Fortnite is integrating real-time ray tracing, AI-powered NVIDIA DLSS, and NVIDIA Reflex technology, significantly enhancing the game's visuals and responsiveness. These advancements will be available across all Fortnite modes, including a new "RTX Treasure Run" creative map designed to showcase the ray tracing effects. The collaboration highlights how NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs are improving competitive gaming with next-level graphics and performance.

title: Micron Unveils GDDR6X Memory For NVIDIA GeForce RTX 30 Series – The Next Chapter In Graphics Memory
summary: Micron has introduced its new GDDR6X memory, designed for NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 30 series graphics cards, specifically the RTX 3090 and RTX 3080. This memory features PAM4 multi-level signaling, doubling the I/O data rate and achieving bandwidths up to 1 TB/s for high-fidelity gaming. GDDR6X also offers improved power efficiency, consuming 15% less power per transferred bit compared to GDDR6, and is expected to reach speeds higher than 21 Gbps in the future.

title: Samsung Electronics lands order to produce next-generation chips for U.S. Nvidia
summary: Samsung Electronics has secured a significant foundry order to produce next-generation graphics processing units (GPUs) for Nvidia, specifically the GeForce RTX 30 Series. This marks a strategic win for Samsung, as Nvidia previously relied on TSMC for its GPU production. The deal leverages Samsung's 8-nano fabrication process, aiming to double GPU performance and challenging TSMC's dominance in the foundry market.

title: NVIDIA sued over 401(k) plan fees
summary: NVIDIA has been sued over fees associated with its 401(k) plan. This news is reported by Pensions & Investments, specializing in lawsuits and legal matters concerning retirement plans.

title: The new 2021 Mercedes S-Class goes tech-tastic
summary: The 2021 Mercedes S-Class is revealed as a technological marvel, featuring advanced infotainment, driver assistance systems, and luxurious interior amenities. Despite a familiar exterior, the car is lighter, more aerodynamic, and includes features like Level 3 autonomy, fingerprint recognition, and extensive customization options. Mercedes also emphasizes the car's environmental consciousness with its production plant and use of recycled materials.

title: China semiconductor-related shares open higher Friday
summary: Chinese semiconductor shares saw significant gains on Friday, with some hitting daily limits, driven by reports that the Chinese government plans to fully support the third-generation semiconductor industry from 2021-2025. This surge is attributed to expectations that the government's 14th five-year plan will accelerate domestic semiconductor growth amidst US restrictions. In contrast, US chipmakers experienced a downturn, with Nvidia, Broadcom, and Qualcomm shares falling.

title: ERISA lawsuit filed against Nvidia; suit against Cornell settled
summary: An ERISA lawsuit has been filed against Nvidia over its 401(k) plan, with plaintiffs alleging excessive investment management fees and a failure to opt for lower-cost share classes. This complaint, filed by Capozzi Adler, mirrors a recent suit against B. Braun Medical. Concurrently, a long-running class-action lawsuit against Cornell University concerning its 403(b) plan has been settled, with terms yet to be disclosed, after allegations of imprudent retention of target-date funds.

title: Office Ready? Jetson-Driven ‘Double Robot’ Supports Remote Working
summary: Double Robotics has launched its third-generation telepresence robot, the Double 3, which is powered by an NVIDIA Jetson TX2 for AI workloads. This update enables advanced autonomous capabilities like improved navigation and obstacle avoidance for remote workers. The robot is designed to provide a physical presence for remote employees in offices, facilitating better interaction and communication, and has seen increased interest due to COVID-19 for contact-free work and international business travel alternatives.

title: NVIDIA and Arm to Create World-Class AI Research Center in Cambridge
summary: NVIDIA and Arm are collaborating to establish a world-class AI research center in Cambridge, UK, which will serve as a hub for AI researchers, scientists, and startups globally. This facility will host an Arm-based supercomputer, provide research fellowships, offer AI training, and support a startup accelerator program. The initiative aims to propel the UK to global AI leadership and foster collaboration in crucial fields like healthcare, autonomous vehicles, and robotics.

title: NVIDIA to Acquire Arm for $40 Billion, Creating World’s Premier Computing Company for the Age of AI
summary: NVIDIA announced it will acquire Arm Limited from SoftBank Group Corp. and the SoftBank Vision Fund for $40 billion. The acquisition aims to create the world's premier computing company for the age of AI, combining NVIDIA’s AI leadership with Arm’s vast computing ecosystem. NVIDIA plans to expand Arm’s R&D presence in Cambridge, UK, establish a world-class AI research and education center, and build an Arm/NVIDIA-powered AI supercomputer, all while maintaining Arm’s open-licensing model and customer neutrality.

title: Highflying Nvidia’s Deal for Arm Signals Loftier Chip Ambition
summary: Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Holdings from SoftBank is poised to significantly impact the global semiconductor industry, further solidifying Nvidia's position. The deal involves a mix of stock and cash, with potential additional payments based on Arm's financial performance. This transaction also marks another major divestment for SoftBank.

title: Duration: 3 minutes, 1 second.
summary: UK tech giant Arm Holdings is being sold to US company Nvidia for $40bn (£31bn) in a deal that faces regulatory approval and opposition from rivals and politicians. Arm co-founder Hermann Hauser heavily criticized the takeover, calling it an "absolute disaster" that would lead to job losses and destroy the company's business model. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pledged to keep Arm headquartered in Cambridge and invest in a new AI research facility there, but the deal raises concerns about Arm's neutrality and its position in the US-China tech rivalry.

title: In a Historic $40 Billion Deal, NVIDIA Acquires Arm Amid Potential Backlash from Chip Industry
summary: NVIDIA has acquired Arm Holdings for $40 billion in a cash and stock deal, aiming to merge Arm's computing ecosystem with NVIDIA's AI leadership. The acquisition, however, faces potential backlash due to concerns about impartiality and neutrality, given NVIDIA's direct competition in the chip industry and Arm's role in licensing architectures to NVIDIA's rivals. Despite assurances from NVIDIA about maintaining Arm's open-licensing model and expanding R&D in the UK, the deal is subject to regulatory approvals and has already sparked political controversy.

title: Nvidia swoops to buy British chipmaker Arm for AI push
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire British chipmaker Arm for US$40bn from SoftBank, consisting of cash and shares. The deal aims to accelerate Nvidia's push into artificial intelligence, leveraging Arm's extensive CPU ecosystem for applications across various industries. While the acquisition is expected to face regulatory and industry scrutiny due to Arm's neutrality among chip producers, Nvidia has pledged to maintain Arm's name, expand its Cambridge base, and establish a new AI research center in the UK.

title: Nvidia Is Buying Arm Holdings From SoftBank in the Largest Ever Chip Deal
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire Arm Holdings from SoftBank Group for approximately $40 billion in a landmark deal involving cash, stock, and future considerations. This acquisition represents the largest chip deal ever. Arm Holdings is a U.K.-based chip design house.

title: Nvidia reaches $40B deal to buy SoftBank's Arm Holdings
summary: Nvidia has agreed to acquire Arm Holdings from SoftBank Group and SoftBank Vision Fund for $40 billion in stock and cash. This deal, which includes $21.5 billion in Nvidia stock and $12 billion cash, aims to position Nvidia strongly in the age of AI, leveraging Arm's processor designs to compete in the data center chip market. SoftBank will retain a less than 10% stake in Arm after the acquisition.

title: Nvidia jumps on $40 billion chip deal; analysts expect tough scrutiny
summary: Nvidia's shares surged after announcing a $40 billion deal to acquire UK-based chip designer Arm from SoftBank, marking a potential shift in the chip industry landscape. Analysts anticipate significant regulatory challenges for the acquisition, particularly from China, due to its scale and implications for competition. The deal is seen as a major move for Nvidia, positioning it among top chip suppliers, but also raising concerns among rivals and regulators.

title: -Nvidia to buy chip designer Arm for $40 bln as SoftBank exits
summary: Nvidia announced its acquisition of UK-based chip designer Arm from SoftBank Group for $40 billion, a deal set to significantly impact the global semiconductor sector. The acquisition poses questions regarding Arm's maintained neutrality under U.S. ownership and faces regulatory scrutiny, particularly in China. Nvidia plans to expand Arm's licensing model and integrate its own IP, while SoftBank exits Arm to raise cash.

title: -Nvidia's Arm deal sparks quick backlash in chip industry
summary: Nvidia's proposed $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd is encountering strong opposition from chip industry rivals in South Korea and China, raising concerns about Arm's neutrality and potential competition with Nvidia. Analysts suggest the deal could be detrimental to Arm's ecosystem and may drive customers toward alternative technologies like RISC-V. Despite Nvidia's assurances of maintaining Arm's open licensing model, competitors fear increased licensing fees and intensified competition in emerging markets like self-driving cars.

title: ARM: Can 'crown jewel' of UK technology be protected?
summary: The UK government is considering options to protect Cambridge-based ARM Holdings after its acquisition by Nvidia, a move that contrasts with their earlier stance during Softbank's purchase in 2016. ARM's co-founder has criticized the deal, fearing Nvidia will disrupt ARM's business model. While Nvidia promises UK investment, blocking the deal poses challenges given current laws and potential impacts on foreign investment.

title: ARM: UK-based chip designer sold to US firm Nvidia
summary: UK-based computer chip designer ARM Holdings has been sold to US firm Nvidia for $40bn (£31.2bn), four years after its acquisition by Softbank. Nvidia has pledged to maintain ARM's UK presence, increase staff, and retain its brand, aiming to create a premier AI computing company. However, the deal faces scrutiny and opposition from ARM's co-founders and others due to concerns about potential conflicts of interest, US export control regulations, and its impact on the UK technology sector.

title: Arm bought from SoftBank by NVIDIA, which plans AI supercomputer
summary: NVIDIA announced its agreement to acquire Arm Ltd. from SoftBank for $40 billion, aiming to combine Arm's semiconductor ecosystem with NVIDIA's AI technology to drive innovation and expand into new markets. NVIDIA plans to establish a new global center of excellence for research in Cambridge, U.K., and build an AI supercomputer. SoftBank will retain an ownership stake in NVIDIA (under 10%) and Arm will continue its open-licensing model and customer neutrality.

title: Why Nvidia is spending $40 billion on Arm
summary: Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm, if completed, would be the largest semiconductor deal ever and is primarily aimed at boosting Nvidia's data center business by integrating Arm's CPU technology with Nvidia's GPUs. The deal raises questions about Nvidia's ability to neutrally license Arm's technology to competitors like Apple and Samsung, but Nvidia plans to operate Arm as an independent, customer-neutral subsidiary. Investors reacted positively to the news, and Nvidia sees significant potential in infusing its AI and graphics chips into Arm's vast ecosystem.

title: Nvidia Confident U.S.-China Tech War Won’t Stop It From Buying Arm
summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence in obtaining regulatory approvals for its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd., despite escalating U.S.-China tech tensions. The deal faces skepticism from Chinese experts and opposition from Arm co-founder Hermann Hauser, who warns of potential job losses and compromised business neutrality. Despite these challenges, Nvidia remains optimistic, citing past regulatory successes.

title: NVIDIA Ampere Architecture Whitepaper Available Now
summary: NVIDIA has released a new whitepaper detailing its Ampere GA102 GPU Architecture, which powers the GeForce RTX 30 Series graphics cards. This comprehensive document provides an in-depth look at the architectural details of their latest GPUs, offering record-breaking performance for PC gamers. Further updates on GeForce GPU performance and features will be shared on GeForce.com.

title: Chip industry wants $50 billion to keep manufacturing in US
summary: The U.S. chip industry is requesting between $20 billion and $50 billion in federal incentives to prevent further manufacturing migration overseas, as other countries, particularly China, heavily invest in semiconductor production. The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) warns that without this investment, the U.S. risks losing its leadership in the sector and jeopardizing national security by relying on foreign supply chains for vital components. The move comes amid increased awareness in Washington regarding supply chain vulnerabilities due to the China-U.S. trade war and the pandemic.

title: A brewing U.S.-China tech cold war rattles the semiconductor industry
summary: The U.S. semiconductor industry is concerned about a brewing tech cold war with China, fearing disruptions to the global supply chain as trade tensions escalate. Companies are developing strategies like hoarding supplies or relocating production, while the U.S. government is pushing for domestic manufacturing incentives through legislation like the CHIPS for America Act and the American Foundries Act. This push aims to strengthen U.S. leadership in advanced technologies and reduce reliance on foreign chip production.

title: The biggest semiconductor deal in history should have been even bigger
summary: Nvidia's acquisition of Arm Holdings for $40 billion marks the semiconductor industry's largest deal, yet Arm's valuation is considered surprisingly low, lagging SoftBank's investment goals. Analysts believe Nvidia's ownership could help Arm realize its full potential, providing resources to a company whose technology is integral to various processors. The deal also highlights Europe's struggle to retain its tech giants, with many being acquired by US companies, though some European firms are now achieving significant market capitalization.

title: MPs to debate Arm Holdings $40bn sale despite Nvidia boss's guarantees
summary: MPs are set to debate the controversial $40bn sale of UK tech firm Arm Holdings to US-based Nvidia, despite Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang offering legally binding guarantees regarding jobs and investment in the UK. Concerns remain among politicians and Arm's co-founder about the potential impact on British interests and the company's neutrality, particularly regarding US legislation. The debate in Parliament aims to press the government for clarity on their stance and actions to safeguard Arm's future.

title: Moore’s Law Is Dead. Long Live Huang’s Law.
summary: This article discusses the decline of Moore's Law and introduces "Huang's Law," named after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang's Law describes the rapid advancement in specialized computing power, particularly for AI applications, driven by GPUs outpacing general-purpose CPUs. The article argues that specialized hardware will be crucial for developing true AI, even as Moore's Law, which predicted the doubling of computing power every 18 months, has reached its limits.

title: Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) To Equip Its Vehicles With NVIDIA’s Orin SoC Chipset To Facilitate Autonomous Driving Under a New Partnership Agreement
summary: Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) has formed a partnership with NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Huizhou Desay SV Automotive to integrate NVIDIA's Orin SoC chipset into its upcoming smart SUV, expected in 2022. This collaboration positions Li Auto to independently develop L4 autonomous driving systems, leveraging Orin's powerful computing capabilities. The move highlights Li Auto's strategic focus on advanced autonomous technology for its Extended-Range Electric Vehicles (EREVs), which are gaining traction in China.

title: There's No Such Thing as 'Huang's Law,' Despite Nvidia's AI Lead
summary: This article disputes the notion of "Huang's Law," which posits that AI silicon performance doubles every two years, similar to Moore's Law. The author argues that this "law" is a misinterpretation that conflates Moore's Law (transistor density) and Dennard scaling (performance per watt), and that Nvidia's AI advancements are heavily reliant on Moore's Law and other technological improvements, not an independent phenomenon. Furthermore, it is too early to declare such a law, and the rate of AI/ML improvement may not be sustainable.

title: Arm CTO on company's small, but vital Silicon Valley presence
summary: Arm Limited's CTO, Dipesh Patel, discussed the company's significant presence in Silicon Valley, despite its smaller size compared to its Cambridge, England office. Arm, which employs around 350 people in San Jose, is set to be acquired by Nvidia Corp. The article highlights the historical roots of Arm's Silicon Valley operations dating back to the mid-1990s.

title: Nvidia's ARM acquisition prompts Ceva upgrade
summary: Northland Capital Markets upgraded semiconductor IP company Ceva to "Outperform" and raised its price target to $48, citing Nvidia's ARM acquisition. Analyst Gus Richard highlights Ceva's strong IP revenue, immunity to the US-China trade war as an Israeli company, exposure to 5G, and potential integration into Apple's future iPhones. The increased valuation reflects the anticipated growth in the semiconductor IP market and a shift towards chiplet models.

title: TSMC To Mass Produce Breakthrough 2nm MBCFET Transistors In 2024
summary: TSMC has achieved a breakthrough in its research and development for the 2nm semiconductor manufacturing node, with plans for trial production in mid-2023 and mass production in 2024. The 2nm process will utilize a new Multi-Bridge Channel Field Effect (MBCFET) transistor design, an evolution over the current FinFET designs and similar to Samsung's approach for its 3nm process. If the projected 90% yield rate for the 2nm process is achieved by 2023, it positions TSMC for a smooth transition to volume production.

title: Skytrac To Make Iridium Certus Terminals
summary: Skytrac Systems is developing new Iridium satcom products, specifically Iridium Certus terminals, designed to support bandwidth-intensive services such as video streaming. The company's SDL-350 Iridium Certus terminal is highlighted as a key product in this new line. This move aims to enhance capabilities for aviation communications.

title: VMware Embraces Nvidia GPUs, DPUs To Drive Enterprise AI
summary: VMware has partnered with Nvidia to integrate GPUs and data processing units (DPUs) into its cloud offerings, aiming to make AI more accessible and easier for enterprises to adopt. The collaboration involves integrating Nvidia's NGC software suite into VMware's virtualization platforms and a broader "Project Monterey" to re-architect VMware's Cloud Foundation with SmartNICs for modern workloads. This initiative seeks to simplify AI deployment, improve performance, and enhance security by making GPUs first-class compute citizens within the VMware ecosystem.

title: Intel Spins Out Omni-Path Interconnect Business Into Stand-Alone Company
summary: Intel has spun out its Omni-Path Architecture high-speed interconnect technology into a new stand-alone company called Cornelis Networks, which has raised $20 million in Series A funding. This move provides an alternative to Nvidia's Mellanox InfiniBand and allows former Intel architects to continue developing and supporting the Omni-Path product line, which Intel had previously de-emphasized. Cornelis Networks aims to support existing customers, sell current products, and develop next-generation interconnect solutions for high-performance computing and AI workloads.

title: Nvidia Offers UK Covid Supercomputer While Waiting on Arm Deal
summary: Nvidia is building a $50 million supercomputer, "Cambridge-1," in the UK to aid COVID-19 healthcare research, offering 400 petaflops of AI computing power to institutions like GlaxoSmithKline and King's College London. This initiative comes as Nvidia awaits government approval for its $40 billion acquisition of British tech company Arm, with regulators scrutinizing potential conditions on job retention in the UK. The supercomputer is described as a non-commercial endeavor to provide much-needed computing resources for researchers.

title: NVIDIA Announces Cloud-AI Video-Streaming Platform to Better Connect Millions Working and Studying Remotely
summary: NVIDIA has launched Maxine, a cloud-AI video-streaming platform designed to enhance video conferencing for millions working and studying remotely. This GPU-accelerated platform enables service providers to offer AI-powered features like super resolution, gaze correction, and noise cancellation, while significantly reducing bandwidth consumption. It leverages cloud-native architecture for scalability and integrates NVIDIA's AI SDKs to improve video and audio quality, making virtual interactions more engaging and efficient.

title: NVIDIA Building UK’s Most Powerful Supercomputer, Dedicated to AI Research in Healthcare
summary: NVIDIA announced it is building Cambridge-1, the UK's most powerful supercomputer, which will be dedicated to AI research in healthcare, including tackling COVID-19.
