title: Google, Microsoft, Qualcomm Protest Nvidia’s Acquisition of Arm Ltd.
summary: Google, Microsoft, and Qualcomm are among several major technology companies that are complaining to U.S. antitrust regulators about Nvidia Corp.'s proposed $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. These companies fear the deal will harm competition in a critical sector of the industry. Some even urge regulators to block the acquisition.

title: Real growth in technology is not from people but machines, says Applied Materials CEO
summary: Applied Materials CEO Gary Dickerson states that the primary driver of technological growth is no longer human data generation, but rather machine-generated data from sensors and the Internet of Things. He notes that the increasing pervasiveness of non-human systems demands more chips and processing power. This shift, accelerated by pandemic-driven virtual presence, signifies a significant and ongoing growth driver for the technology industry, echoing similar sentiments from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

title: Biden Will Order Supply-Chain Review. Chip Stocks Are Surging.
summary: President Joe Biden is expected to sign an executive order to review supply chains in critical industries, including semiconductors. This announcement comes amid a global chip shortage impacting various products from video game consoles to smartphones. Following this news, chip stocks are experiencing a surge.

title: Pliops completes $65 million investment round led by KDT and Nvidia
summary: Pliops, an Israeli cloud storage startup, has successfully closed a $65 million investment round led by Koch Disruptive Technologies and with increased investment from Nvidia, bringing its total capital raised to $115 million. The company, which specializes in developing storage processors to improve data center efficiency, plans to launch its first product in April and aims for significant growth, potentially reaching unicorn status or an IPO. Pliops' technology is designed to address the growing demand for advanced storage and management in data centers by providing rapid and continuous data access.

title: Infographic: Nvidia (NVDA) Q4 revenue up 61%; earnings beat
summary: Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) reported a significant increase in its Q4 revenues and profit, with revenue up 61% and adjusted earnings per share at $3.10, surpassing market expectations. This strong performance, driven by high demand, led to a rise in the company's stock during extended trading.

title: Nvidia sales surge as it struggles to keep gaming chips in stock
summary: Nvidia Corp forecasts better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter revenue, with gaming chips remaining in tight supply due to high global demand and cryptocurrency mining. To counter this, Nvidia is introducing special mining chips and software to discourage miners from using gaming GPUs. The company's aggressive push into AI chips has also contributed to its status as the most valuable semiconductor maker.

title: Introducing the 2021 Adobe Analytics Champions
summary: Adobe announced its 2021 Adobe Analytics Champions program, recognizing 40 individuals for their expertise and dedication to Adobe Analytics. These Champions will participate in career development, knowledge sharing, and provide feedback to Adobe product teams, while also helping other users improve their skills. The program celebrates passionate and knowledgeable Adobe Analytics users globally.

title: Nvidia CEO confident in company's growth prospects even if Arm acquisition does not happen
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence in the company's long-term growth trajectory, even if its acquisition of chip designer Arm is blocked by regulators. Huang emphasized that Nvidia's growth in areas like AI, autonomous vehicles, and 5G edge computing is independent of the Arm deal. Despite this, he remains confident that the $40 billion acquisition of Arm will be completed, believing it will significantly accelerate Arm's roadmap and benefit the ecosystem.

title: Gemini-1 Spreads Millions of Processors Into RAM
summary: GSI Technology introduces Gemini-1, a processor-in-memory chip that accelerates specific mathematical functions by up to 100x compared to traditional processors. Designed as an "associative processing unit" (APU), Gemini-1 integrates about 2 million simple processing elements directly within SRAM cells, making it highly specialized for parallel search and cryptography algorithms. While not a general-purpose CPU, it excels at tasks like Hamming distance and Tanimoto similarity calculations by eliminating the data transfer bottleneck between CPU and RAM.

title: Changing Of The Guard For HPC And Big Iron At HPE
summary: Pete Ungaro, the long-time head of Cray and then HPE's High Performance Computing & Mission Critical Solutions group, is stepping down, with Justin Hotard taking over. This leadership change occurs as HPE continues to navigate a challenging market, focusing on profitability and leveraging the Cray acquisition to scale its HPC business. The company is making strategic bets on services and utility-style pricing for on-premises systems, with recent financial results indicating these efforts are beginning to pay off despite overall revenue and profit declines in some segments.

title: Micron launches automotive-qualified low power DDR5 memory
summary: Micron Technology has introduced the industry's first automotive low-power DDR5 (LPDDR5) DRAM memory, which has been hardware-evaluated to meet the stringent Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) D. This new memory addresses the critical need for robust functional safety in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving, offering increased data access speeds and improved power efficiency. Micron's LPDDR5 is compliant with ISO 26262 standards and includes safety mechanisms to detect and control memory errors, supporting automakers in developing safer vehicles.

title: What Is a Pod? What Is a Cluster?
summary: This article explains the concepts of "pods" and "clusters" in computing, tracing their origins from early data centers to modern AI supercomputers. It highlights how these linked computer systems mimic natural "pods" like those of peas or dolphins, emphasizing their role in providing resilience, scalability, and high performance for internet services and AI applications. The piece also discusses the historical development and the evolution of terminology, showcasing their importance in cloud computing and advanced AI systems like NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD.

title: STMicroelectronics Launches Computer-Vision Launchpad for STM32 MCUs
summary: STMicroelectronics has released a new computer-vision launchpad, including an AI firmware function pack (FP-AI-VISION1) and camera-module hardware, designed for embedded developers using STM32 microcontrollers. This solution enables the creation of affordable, powerful edge-based computer-vision applications by running convolutional neural networks locally. The bundle facilitates image classification, human-presence detection, and offers flexibility for developers to retrain neural networks with custom datasets.

title: Dell Technologies
summary: Equinix and Dell Technologies are collaborating to provide enterprises with flexible and scalable AI infrastructure through cloud-adjacent solutions. This partnership leverages Equinix's global data center footprint and Dell's APEX Flex on Demand to optimize performance, mitigate risk, and offer agile cloud access while controlling IT costs. The offerings include deploying Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA at Equinix's AI-ready facilities to support hybrid multicloud environments.

title: Tech-heavy Nasdaq hits correction with 10.5% fall from peak
summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite has entered correction territory, falling 10.5% from its February peak, as technology shares experienced a significant sell-off. This downturn was driven by concerns over rising bond yields and inflation fears stemming from a new $1.9 trillion COVID-19 relief bill. While financial, restaurant, and travel stocks rose on reopening hopes, they couldn't offset the weight of declining big tech shares like Apple, Nvidia, and Tesla.

title: How Suite It Is: NVIDIA and VMware Deliver AI-Ready Enterprise Platform
summary: NVIDIA and VMware have partnered to optimize VMware vSphere 7 Update 2 for AI applications with the NVIDIA AI Enterprise software suite. This collaboration aims to simplify the development and deployment of AI workloads in hybrid cloud environments, offering scale-out performance and compatibility for a wide range of AI and data science applications. The solution provides enterprises with a comprehensive, optimized, and supported platform for AI, allowing IT professionals to manage AI infrastructure using familiar tools and mitigating risks associated with shadow AI.

title: Is AI Important to Financial Services’ Future? New Survey Says You Can Bank on It
summary: A new NVIDIA survey of over 200 financial services professionals worldwide highlights the growing importance of AI in the industry. Key challenges include a shortage of data scientists and insufficient infrastructure, which firms plan to address by hiring more AI experts.

summary: This article compares the GPU offerings from Nvidia and AMD, focusing on their use in large data centers for tasks like machine learning and high-performance computing. The article concludes by noting Nvidia's lead in AI acceleration, AMD's strong competition in HPC, and the impending entry of Intel into the GPU market.

title: NVIDIA Merlin Accelerates Recommender Workflows with .4 Release
summary: The NVIDIA Merlin .4 release introduces a new API and enhanced inference support to simplify recommender workflows for data scientists and machine learning engineers. Merlin, an open-source framework, leverages deep learning with components like NVTabular, HugeCTR, and Triton Inference Server to build relevant recommenders on large datasets. This update addresses challenges such as slow pipelines and large embedding tables, aiming to accelerate the development and deployment of deep learning recommenders.

title: HP ZBook Firefly 14 G7 review: A compact and durable entry-level mobile workstation
summary: The HP ZBook Firefly 14 G7 is presented as a compact and durable entry-level mobile workstation, featuring a 14-inch display with up to 4K resolution and powered by 10th-generation Intel Core i7 processors with Nvidia Quadro graphics. While praised for its robust build, compact design, and several useful features like a high-quality webcam and comfortable keyboard, its moderate battery life, especially with the 4K screen option, is noted as a drawback. The review highlights its suitability for light mobile workstation tasks but cautions against demanding applications due to battery constraints.

summary: Taiwan's independence is significantly bolstered by its semiconductor industry, particularly Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). TSMC's critical role in the global supply chain for microprocessors provides Taiwan with a strategic advantage, deterring China from invasion due to potential economic repercussions and compelling the United States to protect its access to these vital technologies. summary: Qualcomm Incorporated announced the completion of its acquisition of NUVIA for $1.4 billion. title: Google debuts A2 VMs powered by Nvidia A100 GPUs, its largest cloud instances yet
summary: Google has announced the general availability of its new Compute Engine A2 virtual machines, powered by Nvidia's Ampere A100 Tensor Core GPUs. Designed for demanding machine learning and high-performance computing workloads, Google claims they offer significant performance improvements and cost efficiencies compared to previous generations.

title: AMD says it won't try and stop crypto miners from using its graphics cards
summary: AMD has announced it will not restrict cryptocurrency miners from using its graphics cards, a strategy that contrasts sharply with rival Nvidia's efforts to limit GPU processing power for mining. This decision comes as GPU demand from both gamers and miners has led to frequent shortages. Nvidia previously attempted to curb mining on its RTX 3060 GPU but accidentally released a driver that bypassed the restriction.

title: Intel to Spend $20 Billion on 2 New Chip Factories in Arizona. (Published 2021)
summary: Intel's new CEO, Patrick Gelsinger, announced plans to invest $20 billion in two new chip factories in Arizona. This move signifies Intel's commitment to doubling down on chip manufacturing in the U.S. and Europe, aiming to become a major manufacturer for other companies, addressing concerns about component shortages and reliance on Asian factories. The initiative also seeks to regain Intel's footing in the competitive chip production market, where it had previously fallen behind competitors like TSMC and Samsung.

title: Nintendo to Use Faster Nvidia Chips in New 2021 Switch Model
summary: Nintendo Co. plans to incorporate an upgraded Nvidia Corp. chip with enhanced graphics and processing into a new Switch model for the year-end shopping season. This new iteration will support Nvidia’s Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) technology, allowing for 4K quality visuals when docked to a TV, in addition to an OLED display upgrade. The improvements aim to deliver higher-fidelity graphics more efficiently through AI.

title: Nintendo to use faster Nvidia chips in new 2021 Switch model
summary: Nintendo plans to introduce a new Switch model for the year-end shopping season that will incorporate an upgraded Nvidia chip. This new chip will feature enhanced graphics and processing capabilities, supporting Nvidia’s Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) technology. This will enable the console to display games at 4K quality when connected to a TV and will also include a better CPU and expanded memory, alongside an anticipated 7-inch OLED screen.

summary: This article compares Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) as investments in a market heavily impacted by supply chain issues and increased demand for digital services. summary: Arrow Electronics has finalized an agreement with NVIDIA to distribute its professional visualization product portfolio. The collaboration seeks to accelerate time to market for AI solutions in rapidly evolving sectors like product design, architecture, media, entertainment, and scientific visualization, especially amidst the shift to remote work.

title: China EV maker Nio halts production for 5 days on chip shortage
summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer Nio has announced a five-day halt in production due to a global shortage of semiconductor chips. summary: Hut 8 Mining Corp. has announced a $30 million USD investment in NVIDIA CMPs to significantly boost its mining capabilities, increasing its aggregate operating rate by approximately 1600 Gigahash. summary: Canadian Bitcoin miner Hut 8 has purchased $30 million worth of Nvidia CMPs (GPUs) to expand its mining capabilities beyond just Bitcoin. This move allows for versatility in mining various cryptocurrencies, participation in staking and DeFi, and potential repurposing for High-Performance Computing. The purchase reflects a broader trend among miners to diversify their operations and holdings in the current bull run.

title: US chip giant Nvidia to recruit 600 engineers in Israel to boost AI prowess
summary: Nvidia, the US gaming and computer graphics giant, announced plans to hire 600 hardware and software engineers and chip designers in Israel. This recruitment drive aims to bolster the company's AI-based technologies. Following its acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, Nvidia already employs over 2,400 people across seven R&D centers in Israel, making it the company's largest R&D operation outside the US.

title: Chip giant Nvidia set to recruit 600 new employees in Israel
summary: Chipmaking giant Nvidia plans to recruit 600 new employees in Israel across its local development centers, primarily for software specialization. This move follows its 2019 acquisition of Mellanox and intensifies the competition for tech talent in the country. Nvidia's Israeli development center is the largest outside the U.S., and the company is heavily involved in the local startup ecosystem.

title: Integrating with Telephone Networks to Enable Real-Time AI Services
summary: Ribbon Communications, in collaboration with NVIDIA, developed a solution to analyze contact center calls in real-time using advanced AI. The Ribbon AI gateway acts as a secure bridge converting Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) audio streams into an AI-acceptable audio format for transcription and analysis. This architecture allows businesses to dynamically control call handling using REST APIs for applications like regulatory compliance, fraud analysis, and sentiment analysis, addressing critical limitations of delayed call recording analysis.

title: Arm unveils Armv9 architecture for its next generation of processor chips
summary: Arm Holdings Ltd. has introduced its new Armv9 CPU architecture, the first major update in a decade, focusing on enhanced performance and security. The architecture is optimized for specialized workloads like AI and digital signal processing, integrating Scalable Vector Expansion technology to achieve over 30% performance gains in future mobile and server chips. Armv9 also features a Confidential Compute Architecture with "Realms" to secure data during processing, addressing a critical need for end-to-end data security in modern computing environments.

title: Arm’s v9 Architecture Explains Why Nvidia Needs To Buy It
summary: This article explores why Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Holdings, initially questioned, makes strategic sense following Arm's v9 architecture announcement. The v9 architecture's focus on integrating vector math, matrix math, and digital signal processing into CPUs, alongside new security features and a "Realms" memory partitioning system, suggests a future where specialized, highly integrated compute on-device is paramount. Nvidia's move to acquire Arm is positioned as a bet on this evolving compute landscape, where a single, malleable architecture can support a vast array of devices from IoT to datacenters, potentially limiting the expansion of hybrid CPU-GPU models for certain workloads.

title: Volvo partners with Aurora for hub-to-hub autonomous trucking
summary: Volvo Group has selected Aurora as its primary technology partner for developing autonomous, hub-to-hub trucking solutions in North America, making it the last major truck manufacturer to choose such a partner. This partnership builds on previous quiet collaborations since 2018 and aims to integrate Aurora's Driver software with Volvo's technology for a "trucking-as-a-service" model. Aurora continues to expand its portfolio, having recently acquired Uber's Advanced Technologies Group and partnering with PACCAR.

title: What HR tools are NVIDIA using to hire 600 Israelis?
summary: NVIDIA is set to hire 600 new employees in Israel, increasing its headcount by 25%. Gideon Rosenberg, NVIDIA's HR leader, discusses the tools and strategies they use for recruitment, including Textio for inclusive job descriptions and LinkedIn Recruiter licenses. The company also shares its experience adapting to the pandemic, its plans for onboarding new hires, and its intention to adopt a hybrid work model post-Covid-19.

title: Taiwan chip giant plans big investment as rivalry intensifies
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) announced plans to invest US$100 billion over the next three years to significantly expand its chip fabrication capacity. This massive investment comes as the company faces booming demand for advanced semiconductors and aims to maintain its leading position in the industry amid a global chip supply crunch. Other major players like Intel and Samsung are also heavily investing in semiconductor foundries to meet increasing demand.

title: Hyundai likely to briefly halt 2nd plant; Grandeur sedan affected
summary: Hyundai Motor Co. plans to briefly suspend operations at its Asan plant from April 7 due to a shortage of power control units (PCUs), affecting production of Sonata and Grandeur sedans. This is the second plant suspension announced by Hyundai, following a similar halt at its Ulsan plant for issues with chips for Kona SUVs and PE modules for IONIQ 5s. The widespread disruptions highlight the automotive industry's increasing dependence on semiconductors for various vehicle technologies.

title: Intel Launches Its Most Advanced Performance Data Center Platform
summary: Intel has launched its 3rd Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors (code-named “Ice Lake”), marking its most advanced performance data center platform. These processors offer an average 46% increase in performance for popular data center workloads, alongside built-in AI acceleration and advanced security features. The platform is optimized for a broad range of applications across cloud, network, and intelligent edge environments, with significant industry adoption already underway.

title: Good Signs for MoonShine: Animation Studio Elevates Virtual Production and Collaboration With NVIDIA Omniverse
summary: MoonShine Animation, a leading Taiwanese animation and VFX company, successfully adopted NVIDIA Omniverse and RTX Virtual Workstation during the COVID-19 pandemic to enable remote work and enhance virtual production. The integration of NVIDIA technologies streamlined their workflow, making virtual production more practical and efficient.

title: The Alienware m15 Ryzen Edition R5 is an AMD-NVIDIA combo over a decade in the making
summary: The Alienware m15 Ryzen Edition R5 is announced, marking the first Alienware notebook in over a decade to combine AMD processors with NVIDIA graphics. It will be available starting April 7th in China, April 20th in the US, and May 4th globally, with select configurations beginning at $1793.98.

title: Nvidia announces Omniverse Enterprise suite for real-time, photorealistic graphics design
summary: Nvidia introduced Omniverse Enterprise, a new suite designed for real-time collaborative 3D design and graphics rendering. This platform enables geographically dispersed teams to work together on complex projects, leveraging photorealistic rendering and real-time ray tracing. Key components include Omniverse Nucleus, Connectors for third-party apps, and Nvidia's own Create and View applications, with companies like BMW Group and Ericsson already using it for digital twin creation and 5G network simulation.

title: Nvidia debuts Grace, its first data center CPU for advanced AI workloads
summary: Nvidia has launched Grace, its first Arm-based data center CPU, specifically designed to handle the demanding requirements of advanced AI workloads like natural language processing and drug discovery. Grace is intended to work in conjunction with Nvidia's GPUs to deliver significantly higher performance than current systems, and will power future supercomputers like the Alps project at the Swiss National Computing Center. The company also announced other AI initiatives, including the cloud-native DGX SuperPOD and the Jarvis conversational AI framework.

title: Nvidia steps up competition with Intel and AMD with first data-center CPU, based on Arm
summary: Nvidia introduced its first data-center CPU, named Grace, based on Arm technology, aiming to intensify its competition with Intel and AMD in the artificial-intelligence market. This move signals Nvidia's commitment to the chip-making sector, leveraging technology from its acquisition target, Arm Holdings PLC, to tap into the growing AI business. The announcement was made during Nvidia’s annual GTC developers conference by CEO Jensen Huang.

title: Nvidia to directly challenge Intel with Arm-based 'Grace' server chip
summary: Nvidia Corp announced its plan to develop an Arm-based server processor chip called "Grace," directly challenging Intel in the data center market. This move intensifies competition with Intel and adds complexity to the antitrust review of Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm. The new server chip, expected in 2023, is designed for artificial intelligence algorithms, further solidifying Nvidia's focus on AI computing.

title: Swiss National Supercomputing Centre, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and NVIDIA Announce World’s Most Powerful AI-Capable Supercomputer
summary: The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), and NVIDIA announced the creation of "Alps," which is expected to be the world's most powerful AI-capable supercomputer when it comes online in 2023. This system will replace CSCS’s existing Piz Daint supercomputer and serve a broad community of researchers, offering 7x faster AI capabilities than current leading systems. Alps will be built by HPE using the new HPE Cray EX supercomputer product line, featuring NVIDIA HGX supercomputing platform including NVIDIA GPUs and the new Arm-based NVIDIA Grace CPU, enabling breakthrough research across various scientific fields.

title: NVIDIA and Global Computer Makers Launch Industry-Standard Enterprise Server Platforms for AI
summary: NVIDIA introduced new NVIDIA-Certified Systems designed to bring AI capabilities to organizations using industry-standard enterprise data center infrastructure. These systems, featuring NVIDIA AI Enterprise software certified for VMware vSphere 7, allow businesses to run virtualized AI applications on existing servers. The launch includes new NVIDIA A30 and A10 GPUs to support mainstream AI and graphics workloads, with computer makers like Atos, Dell Technologies, and Supermicro offering these NVIDIA EGX platform-enabled servers.

title: NVIDIA Announces CPU for Giant AI and High Performance Computing Workloads
summary: NVIDIA has announced its first data center CPU, Grace, an Arm-based processor designed to deliver 10x the performance of today’s fastest servers for complex AI and high-performance computing workloads. This specialized processor targets advanced applications with enormous datasets and massive memory requirements, making NVIDIA a "three-chip company" alongside its GPUs and DPUs. The Swiss National Supercomputing Centre and Los Alamos National Laboratory are among the first to plan Grace-powered supercomputers, expected online in 2023.

title: NVIDIA Partners with Schrödinger to Further Accelerate Drug Discovery Worldwide
summary: NVIDIA is partnering with Schrödinger to accelerate drug discovery by integrating Schrödinger's computational platform with NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD systems and NVIDIA Clara Discovery. This collaboration aims to enhance the speed and accuracy of evaluating billions of molecules for therapeutics, making advanced drug discovery tools accessible to the entire pharmaceutical industry, from startups to multinational corporations. The initiative will leverage NVIDIA's GPU technology to optimize Schrödinger's physics-based modeling and machine learning capabilities.

title: The future of work, phase two: what to expect
summary: Cisco leaders and customers discuss the future of work, emphasizing how cloud technology, improved communication, and hybrid models will shape a more flexible, inclusive, and secure environment. The pandemic accelerated the adoption of these changes, highlighting the importance of digital agility, employee well-being, and seamless, secure collaborative experiences for businesses, education, and healthcare.

title: Nvidia Reveals Arm-Based Data Center CPU To Take On Intel, AMD
summary: Nvidia has unveiled Grace, an Arm-based data center CPU designed to compete with Intel and AMD in AI and high-performance computing. Grace, expected in early 2023, promises 10 times faster AI performance than AMD's EPYC CPUs and is a key component of Nvidia's expanded data center strategy, which now includes GPUs, DPUs, and CPUs. This move comes as Nvidia progresses with its acquisition of Arm and aims to provide an optimal architecture for trillion-parameter AI models.

title: Cisco, Salesforce take top 2 spots in Fortune's 2021 Best Companies to Work For list
summary: Cisco and Salesforce secured the top two positions on Fortune's 2021 Best Companies to Work For list. Despite narratives of an exodus from the Bay Area, nearly 20% of the companies recognized on Fortune's list for 2021 are headquartered in the region. Intuit, headquartered in Mountain View, also made it to the list at the No. 11 spot.

title: Lloyds Shares: Dividend Outlook for 2022 and 2023
summary: This article examines the dividend outlook for Lloyds shares for 2022 and 2023, analyzing its recent share price performance and future dividend payments. It details the interim 2022 dividend and predicts the final 2022 dividend's ex-dividend and payment dates, along with implications for investors. The article also provides historical dividend data and context regarding the PRA's previous directive to suspend bank dividends during the pandemic.

title: NVIDIA Announces New DGX SuperPOD, the First Cloud-Native, Multi-Tenant Supercomputer, Opening World of AI to Enterprise
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled the new DGX SuperPOD, a cloud-native, multi-tenant AI supercomputer incorporating NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPUs for enhanced security and performance. This system, along with NVIDIA Base Command software, allows enterprises to securely share and operate their AI infrastructure for diverse applications like conversational AI, drug discovery, and autonomous vehicles. NVIDIA also introduced a subscription offering for the DGX Station A100, aiming to make AI development more accessible to a broader range of businesses and research institutions.

title: NVIDIA Launches Omniverse Design Collaboration and Simulation Platform for Enterprises
summary: NVIDIA has announced the general availability of NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise, a platform enabling global 3D design teams to collaborate in real-time within a shared virtual space. This platform facilitates seamless work on complex projects for geographically dispersed teams, eliminating the need for in-person meetings or file exchanges. Major companies like BMW Group, Foster + Partners, and WPP are already leveraging Omniverse Enterprise for applications ranging from factory digital twins to virtual ad production, highlighting its transformative potential across various industries.

title: NVIDIA Extends Data Center Infrastructure Processing Roadmap with BlueField-3
summary: NVIDIA announced its next-generation data processing unit (DPU), BlueField-3, designed to provide advanced software-defined networking, storage, and cybersecurity acceleration for data centers. Optimized for AI and cloud-native environments, BlueField-3 offloads up to 300 CPU cores worth of infrastructure services, creating "zero-trust" environments. The DPU is supported by the NVIDIA DOCA SDK and is being integrated by major server manufacturers and cloud service providers.

title: NVIDIA Unveils NVIDIA DRIVE Atlan, an AI Data Center on Wheels for Next-Gen Autonomous Vehicles
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled NVIDIA DRIVE Atlan, its next-generation AI-enabled processor for autonomous vehicles, designed to deliver over 1,000 trillion operations per second (TOPS) for automakers' 2025 models. This system-on-a-chip integrates AI and software with advanced computing, networking, and security, including an NVIDIA BlueField DPU for data-center-grade security. DRIVE Atlan will provide robust compute capabilities for software-defined, upgradeable vehicles and extends NVIDIA's DRIVE family alongside existing Xavier and Orin processors.

title: Top Robotaxi Companies Hail Rides on NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: NVIDIA's CEO Jensen Huang announced at GTC that several leading robotaxi companies, including Cruise, Zoox, DiDi, Oxbotica, Pony.ai, and AutoX, are developing their Level 4/5 autonomous systems using the NVIDIA DRIVE platform. The article emphasizes the significant opportunity for robotaxis to transform transportation by providing safer and more efficient mobility services, projecting that they could account for over 5% of global vehicle miles traveled by 2030. These companies leverage NVIDIA's high-performance, end-to-end AI compute capabilities to manage the immense data and software complexity required for fully autonomous operations.

title: NVIDIA Launches Morpheus to Bring AI-Driven Automation to Cybersecurity Industry
summary: NVIDIA has introduced Morpheus, an AI-driven application framework designed to enhance cybersecurity by providing accelerated AI capabilities for real-time threat detection and prevention. This framework, powered by NVIDIA GPUs and BlueField DPUs, enables comprehensive monitoring of data center transactions and allows organizations to analyze all network packets at line-rate speed. Morpheus aims to help cybersecurity providers develop AI solutions that can instantly detect and eliminate sophisticated cyber breaches, collaborating with industry leaders to integrate these advanced offerings.

title: NVIDIA CEO Introduces Software, Silicon, Supercomputers ‘for the Da Vincis of Our Time’
summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang unveiled a comprehensive vision for the future at GTC, highlighting advancements in AI, automotive, robotics, and virtual worlds. He introduced new hardware like the Grace data center CPU, BlueField-3 DPU, and NVIDIA Atlan for automotive, alongside significant software developments such as NVIDIA AI, Omniverse, and various AI acceleration libraries. Huang emphasized NVIDIA's evolution into a computing platform company offering solutions across GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs, and a robust software ecosystem to empower researchers and enterprises.

title: Drug Discovery Gets Jolt of AI via NVIDIA Collaborations with AstraZeneca, U of Florida Health
summary: NVIDIA is collaborating with AstraZeneca and UF Health on AI research projects using transformer neural networks to accelerate drug discovery. AstraZeneca is developing a generative AI model for chemical structures with NVIDIA's Cambridge-1 supercomputer, while UF Health is using NVIDIA’s Megatron framework to create GatorTron, a large clinical language model. These initiatives, along with new NGC applications and partnerships, aim to leverage AI and supercomputing to speed up pharmaceutical research and medical innovation.

title: Volvo Cars, Zoox, SAIC and More Join Growing Range of Autonomous Vehicle Makers Using New NVIDIA DRIVE Solutions
summary: NVIDIA announced that its NVIDIA DRIVE solutions are being adopted by a growing number of leading transportation companies, including Volvo Cars, Zoox, and SAIC, for next-generation AI-based autonomous vehicles. The company's design-win pipeline for NVIDIA DRIVE now exceeds $8 billion over the next six years, covering various vehicle types from cars to robotaxis and new energy vehicles. Volvo Cars will use NVIDIA DRIVE Orin in its upcoming XC90, while other companies like Zoox, DiDi, Faraday Future, VinFast, Nio, Li Auto, Xpeng, Navistar, FAW, and Volvo Autonomous Solutions are also integrating NVIDIA DRIVE for advanced autonomous capabilities in their vehicles.

title: An Engine of Innovation: Sony Levels Up for the AI Era
summary: Sony is significantly enhancing its AI capabilities by installing an NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD in its R&D Center to accelerate machine learning efforts across its diverse product portfolio. This move allows internal developers to focus on AI innovation without cloud cost concerns, leading to faster training times for advanced applications like super-resolution imaging. Sony is leveraging NVIDIA's hardware and software, including NGC containers and CUDA, to power its AI pipeline for products ranging from smartphones and robotics to imaging chips and professional drones.

title: Data processing units accelerate infrastructure performance
summary: Data processing units (DPUs) are emerging as a critical technology in data centers, offloading networking and communication tasks from CPUs to enhance infrastructure performance. This article explains how DPUs work, highlights key vendors like Fungible, Nvidia, AWS, and Nebulon, and discusses their role in software-defined infrastructure and future enterprise adoption.

title: NVIDIA, BMW Blend Reality, Virtual Worlds to Demonstrate Factory of the Future
summary: NVIDIA and BMW are collaborating to create future factories using digital twins and NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise. This technology enables global 3D design teams to work together in a shared virtual space, integrating AI, robotics, and edge computing. The collaboration aims to revolutionize manufacturing processes by improving planning efficiency, worker ergonomics, and robotic automation, ultimately reducing planning times by 30%.

title: Synopsys Tackles SoC Design with Unified Circuit Simulation Flow
summary: Synopsys has launched PrimeSim Continuum, a unified circuit simulation workflow designed to address the increasing complexity and scale of heterogeneous System-on-Chip (SoC) designs across various applications. This all-in-one solution integrates multiple simulation engines including PrimeSim SPICE, PrimeSim Pro, PrimeSim HSPICE, and PrimeSim XA, providing a seamless simulation experience with improved productivity and ease of use. PrimeSim Continuum leverages next-generation architectures and heterogeneous computing to optimize resource utilization, aiming to reduce verification times from days to hours, as demonstrated by early access customers like Kioxia and partners like Samsung and Nvidia.

title: NVIDIA Sets AI Inference Records, Introduces A30 and A10 GPUs for Enterprise Servers
summary: NVIDIA announced its AI inference platform, featuring new A30 and A10 GPUs for mainstream servers, has achieved record-setting performance in all MLPerf benchmark categories. These GPUs offer high performance and low power consumption for enterprise AI inference, training, graphics, and traditional computing workloads, with major server manufacturers expected to integrate them soon. The platform's success highlights NVIDIA's commitment to democratizing AI, extended by its software stack and Multi-Instance GPU capability.

title: Cultivating AI: AgTech Industry Taps NVIDIA GPUs to Protect the Planet
summary: The agricultural technology (AgTech) industry is increasingly using NVIDIA GPUs to tackle critical environmental and agricultural challenges. Startups and researchers are deploying AI-powered solutions, from protecting bee colonies from parasites and preventing crop diseases like citrus greening, to reducing chemical use through precision spraying and improving dairy farm efficiency. This move demonstrates a significant positive social impact, leveraging AI to address issues ranging from food security to environmental sustainability.

title: Leaked tests show Nvidia's CMP 40HX mining card performing close to an RTX 3060
summary: Nvidia's CMP 40HX mining card is reportedly performing close to an RTX 3060 in leaked tests. Asus was able to optimize the card's hash rate for Ethereum mining to over 43 MH/s, a significant increase from the advertised 36 MH/s. This improved performance, combined with a projected retail price of around $699, might encourage miners to purchase the CMP 40HX instead of the consumer-geared RTX 3060, leaving more RTX 3060 cards available for gamers.

title: Arm details new data center chips, says Oracle, Alibaba will use them
summary: Arm Ltd revealed new details about its next-generation data center technology, with its "N2" Neoverse computing cores expected to be about 40% faster and "V1" cores 50% faster than previous methods for AI tasks. Oracle Corp and Alibaba Group Holding are set to use these new Arm-based chips, signaling a growing push into the data center processor market long dominated by Intel and AMD. This move is seen as crucial for Nvidia Corp's $40 billion acquisition of Arm, which is currently under national security review.

title: Intel vs Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
summary: This article analyzes the long-standing rivalry between Intel and AMD, comparing their historical market dominance, recent performance, financial health, and future outlook. It highlights AMD's recent surge due to TSMC's advanced chip manufacturing, challenging Intel's traditional leadership. The author concludes by positioning AMD as a growth play and Intel as a value play, considering potential comebacks and ongoing industry challenges like chip shortages.

title: Arm Puts Some Muscle Into Future Neoverse Server CPU Designs
summary: Arm is unveiling details about its future Neoverse V1 ("Zeus") and N2 ("Perseus") server CPU designs, aimed at the datacenter and edge. The V1 core is designed for high-performance computing and enterprise workloads, offering significantly better single-threaded integer performance than its predecessor, while the N2 core optimizes for performance per dollar and watt, targeting mainstream infrastructure servers. These new designs, based on the upcoming Armv9-A architecture, highlight Arm's continued push into the server market with tailored solutions.

title: Apple Finally Feels the Effects of the Global Chip Shortage
summary: Apple Inc. reported strong revenue and record sales in its latest quarter, but warned that the global chip shortage is beginning to impact its business. Executives stated that supply constraints would specifically affect iPad and Mac sales, potentially reducing third-quarter revenue by $3 billion to $4 billion. This marks the first significant impact of the chip shortage on Apple's previously resilient production.

title: Crypto ETF | Invest in the Crypto Revolution
summary: VanEck offers a Crypto ETF (VanEck Blockchain and Crypto Innovators UCITS ETF) designed for investors looking to gain diversified exposure to the rapidly growing blockchain ecosystem. This ETF provides a pure-play approach by investing in companies driving the crypto evolution across various sectors like payment gateways, hardware, exchanges, crypto miners, and blockchain services. The article details the ETF's specifications, rationale for investing, and potential risks associated with the asset class.

title: Crypto ETF | Invest in the Crypto Revolution
summary: The VanEck Crypto ETF (VanEck Blockchain and Crypto Innovators UCITS ETF) offers investors a diversified and pure-play approach to invest in the rapidly growing blockchain ecosystem. It targets companies involved in various sectors like payment gateways, hardware, exchanges, crypto mining, crypto holding/trading, blockchain patents/services, and banking/asset management. The ETF focuses on liquid, innovative companies worldwide with a dynamic composition reviewed quarterly, while also highlighting the inherent risks associated with such investments, including liquidity, limited diversification, and risks related to smaller companies.

title: Apple’s new M1 chip creates a competitive advantage
summary: Apple has introduced new iMacs and iPad Pros featuring its M1 chip, allowing the company to control its entire technology stack and gain a competitive advantage. This strategy insulates Apple from the global chip shortage affecting other manufacturers reliant on third-party semiconductors. Experts like Richard Barnett highlight that Apple's approach contrasts sharply with the challenges faced by automotive, consumer electronics, and medical device industries.

title: Intel’s $3.5B New Mexico Campus Upgrade To Boost Next-Gen Chips
summary: Intel is investing $3.5 billion to upgrade its New Mexico manufacturing site, enabling it to produce next-generation processors with Foveros 3D packaging technology. This investment is part of Intel's new IDM 2.0 strategy, which aims to enhance performance, create jobs, and regain leadership in the chip market. The Foveros technology will allow Intel to stack chip tiles vertically, offering greater flexibility and performance in a smaller footprint.

title: Intel to Spend USD $3.5 Billion to Upgrade New Mexico Factory; More Exciting Chips Soon?
summary: Intel plans to invest $3.5 billion to upgrade its New Mexico factory, aiming to boost domestic chip manufacturing and address the global semiconductor shortage. This move is also a strategic response to competitors like AMD, enabling potentially lower chip costs and increased availability of upcoming products such as the 12th Gen Alder Lake processors and a powerful gaming-grade Xe-HPG graphics card. Intel's investment signals a push towards innovation and expanded in-house production, including custom chips for third-party clients.

title: NVIDIA Merlin Latest Enhancements Streamlines Recommender Workflows with .5 Release | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: NVIDIA Merlin's .5 update introduces key enhancements to streamline recommender workflows for machine learning engineers. The update includes a configurable data generator for training, a multi-GPU dataloader, and initial support for session-based recommenders, which are gaining attention for their ability to increase prediction accuracy with dynamic user interests. These additions reinforce NVIDIA's commitment to democratizing and accelerating the development of effective recommender systems.

title: These Were Nvidia’s 5 Most Highly Compensated Executives Last Year
summary: Nvidia's top five executives received higher compensation in fiscal year 2021, largely due to increased stock awards and incentive pay tied to the company's strong performance in data center and gaming markets. CEO Jensen Huang was the most compensated, earning $19.3 million, with his and other executives' base salaries slightly increasing due to an extra week in the fiscal year. The article details the compensation breakdown for each of the five highest-paid executives, highlighting the significant growth in their total earnings compared to the previous year.

title: STMicroelectronics Tackles the EV Industry with GaN
summary: STMicroelectronics is focusing on gallium nitride (GaN) technology to enhance efficiency in electric vehicle applications, recognizing its superiority over silicon in high-power scenarios. The company has released a new family of GaN devices called STi2GaN, specifically designed for the automotive industry, which integrates power stages, drivers, and protection within GaN and SiP solutions. This move aligns with STMicroelectronics' earlier commitment to invest in wide-bandgap semiconductors for carbon neutrality goals.

title: Redwood City startup Mythic scores $70M to challenge Nvidia on AI chips
summary: Redwood City-based startup Mythic has successfully raised $70 million to further develop its AI chips, positioning itself to challenge market leader Nvidia. Mythic is part of a new wave of semiconductor companies aiming to create chips that outperform existing options for AI tasks. This funding round highlights increasing competition in the AI chip market.

title: Z by HP Powers Creative Collaboration Everywhere for Today’s Creators
summary: HP has introduced new ZBook Studio G8, ZBook Fury G8, and ZBook Power G8 mobile workstations, designed for professional creators and power users who need performance, reliability, and versatility in hybrid work environments. These new models offer powerful computing, collaborative tools like ZCentral Remote Boost, and enhanced security features, while also emphasizing sustainability through the use of recycled materials and energy-efficient manufacturing. The ZBook Studio G8 is highlighted as the most powerful mobile workstation of its size, the ZBook Fury G8 as the most expandable and customizable, and the ZBook Power G8 provides an affordable professional-grade option.

title: 10 Hot Data Center Technologies And Trends To Watch In 2021
summary: This article outlines ten significant data center technologies and trends for 2021, driven by the shift to remote work and a digital economy. Key themes include the rise of "as-a-service" models, massive investments by public cloud providers, increasing private equity in data centers, and heightened CPU innovation from Intel, AMD, and Nvidia. Additionally, the article highlights the growing importance of automation, sustainability, and edge computing in the data center industry.

title: NVIDIA Transforms Mainstream Laptops into Gaming Powerhouses with GeForce RTX 30 Series
summary: NVIDIA has launched a new line of GeForce RTX laptops, powered by the RTX 3050 Ti and 3050 Laptop GPUs, making real-time ray tracing and AI-based DLSS accessible to more gamers and creators starting at $799. These new laptops offer significant performance improvements, including being twice as fast as previous-generation systems, and introduce features like NVIDIA Reflex for low-latency esports and NVIDIA Broadcast for enhanced video conferencing and livestreaming. NVIDIA Studio laptops with RTX 30 Series GPUs also offer up to 2x faster performance for creative applications, empowering artists and video editors.

title: WeRide reaches series C at $3.3bn valuation
summary: WeRide, a China-based autonomous driving technology provider, has secured hundreds of millions of dollars in Series C funding, valuing the company at $3.3 billion. The capital will be used for research and development and commercialization activities. Investors in this round include IDG Capital, Homeric Capital, and Qiming Venture Partners, among others, following previous investments from companies like Yutong Group, SenseTime, and Nvidia.

title: Insiders reveal one big surprise about a rumored OLED Nintendo Switch Pro
summary: Rumors suggest an OLED Nintendo Switch Pro is in the works, with industry insiders weighing in on what an OLED screen and a more powerful CPU could mean for the new console. While some believe an OLED screen is a natural evolution and won't significantly impact price, others see it and a new CPU as major upgrades that will improve the handheld experience. The article highlights the speculative nature of these discussions, despite enthusiasm from fans.

title: S Korea unveils US$450bn chipmaking master plan
summary: South Korea has announced a monumental US$450 billion investment plan over the next decade to build the world’s largest chipmaking base, involving key players like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. This initiative, dubbed the "K-semiconductor belt," aims to boost semiconductor research and production, enhance the nation's advanced logic chip capabilities, and reduce reliance on external manufacturers, amidst a global race for chip dominance and ongoing supply shortages. The government will support the industry with significant tax breaks, infrastructure improvements, and training programs to compete with global leaders like TSMC.

title: Three Partners Named Top Rising Stars in M&A by The Deal
summary: Latham & Watkins partners Daniel Breslin, Saad Khanani, and Victoria VanStekelenburg have been recognized by The Deal as "Top Rising Stars: Class of 2021" in Mergers & Acquisitions. The article highlights their significant contributions to major M&A transactions, their individual deal-making philosophies, and their involvement in firm initiatives like training and diversity. Each partner shared insights into what drives their engagement and success in the M&A field.

title: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks Deliver Unprecedented Firewall Performance for 5G Cloud-Native Security with DPU Acceleration
summary: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks have partnered to create a high-performance cybersecurity solution for 5G cloud-native environments. Their joint offering combines the Palo Alto Next-Generation Firewall with the NVIDIA BlueField-2 Data Processing Unit (DPU) to achieve up to 100Gb/s throughput with 80% traffic offload. This collaboration results in a 6X throughput increase over traditional host-based firewall solutions, addressing the demanding security needs of modern 5G networks.

title: Nvidia sets 4-for-1 stock split, shares rise
summary: Nvidia Corp announced a four-for-one stock split to make its shares more affordable for investors, causing its stock to rise by 3%. This move follows similar splits by Apple and Tesla last year, with Nvidia's split requiring stockholder approval in June and effective mid-July.

title: NVIDIA Announces Four-for-One Stock Split, Pending Stockholder Approval at Annual Meeting Set for June 3
summary: NVIDIA announced a four-for-one stock split in the form of a stock dividend, pending stockholder approval at its annual meeting on June 3. The split aims to make stock ownership more accessible to investors and employees. If approved, stockholders of record on June 21, 2021, will receive three additional shares for every share held, with trading on a split-adjusted basis expected to begin on July 20.

title: Putting the Chip Shortage into the Context of Long-Term Trends
summary: The article analyzes the current global semiconductor shortage, attributing it to supply chain rigidities, high barriers to entry, and geopolitical tensions exacerbated by COVID-19. It highlights the long-term trends driving increased semiconductor demand, such as 5G, AI, and electric vehicles, and discusses how governments and companies are responding to secure future supply chains and potentially re-shore manufacturing.

title: May 2021 Product Update -What’s New
summary: The May 2021 Fusion 360 product update introduces several new features and improvements across usability, sketching & modeling, electronics, generative design, and manufacturing. Key enhancements include Augmented Reality support via USDz export, a revamped Learning Panel, and expanded learning content for Fusion 360 Extensions. The update also brings significant advancements in electronics design with Stop Mask support in 3D PCB, improved display dialogs, and new library parts, alongside new generative design capabilities like Transparent View and enhanced manufacturing support for Formlabs and SLM Solutions 3D printers, plus machine simulation as a preview feature.

title: Samsung, TSMC up ante in US foundry competition
summary: The world's two largest foundry chipmakers, TSMC and Samsung Electronics, are engaged in fierce competition to expand their presence in the US, driven by significant investment plans. Samsung announced a $17 billion investment for a US factory, following TSMC's $12 billion Arizona plant. This rivalry, coupled with Intel's entry into the foundry business, intensifies the competition in the advanced chip manufacturing market, with both companies risking substantial losses if they fail to secure enough clients for their costly new facilities.

title: SOXX Versus SOXL Semiconductor ETF Forecast: Which Is a Better Buy?
summary: This article compares two semiconductor ETFs, SOXX and SOXL, to determine which might be a better investment. SOXL is a leveraged ETF offering 3x daily returns, leading to higher performance during bull markets but also higher risk. SOXX is a plain ETF for risk-averse, long-term investors, with both ETFs holding similar top companies and having a positive medium-term outlook despite the cyclical nature of the industry.

title: Nvidia sold $155 million in crypto mining chips last quarter, but PC gaming remains its biggest market
summary: Nvidia reported $155 million in revenue from its new cryptocurrency mining processors (CMPs) in the last quarter, with projected sales of $400 million for the current quarter. Despite these figures, CEO Jensen Huang emphasizes that PC gaming remains the company's primary and most important market, generating $2.76 billion in revenue. The introduction of CMP chips is intended to protect the supply of graphics cards for gamers by diverting crypto miners from purchasing gaming-specific GPUs.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2022
summary: NVIDIA reported record revenue of $5.66 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2022, an 84% increase year-over-year, driven by strong growth in its Gaming and Data Center platforms. The company also announced a four-for-one stock split and provided an optimistic outlook for the second quarter, projecting revenue of $6.30 billion. Key highlights include advancements in Gaming with new RTX GPUs and DLSS adoption, and significant innovations in Data Center and Automotive sectors.

title: Stock of the week - NVIDIA (27.05.2021)
summary: NVIDIA (NVDA.US) reported record first-quarter fiscal 2022 results, exceeding revenue and EPS expectations, driven by strong performance in Gaming, Data Center, and Professional Visualization platforms. The company also announced an upbeat Q2 forecast and a 4-for-1 stock split, which is seen as a bullish signal for investors. The growth is significantly boosted by the gaming sector during the pandemic and the increasing demand for its graphics cards by cryptocurrency miners.

title: Vision Fund loss slashes Masayoshi Son’s 2020 salary by 52%
summary: SoftBank Group founder and CEO Masayoshi Son's salary was more than halved in 2020 to 100 million yen ($0.9 million), a 52% decrease from 2019, largely attributed to the Vision Fund's substantial losses in the 2019 financial year. However, with SoftBank posting a record-breaking net profit of 4.99 trillion yen in FY 2020, Son's salary is anticipated to rebound significantly in the current year. The article also notes recent investments by SoftBank's Vision Fund in companies like Yanolja and Balance Hero.

title: How Nvidia plans to own the data center with AI
summary: Nvidia aims to revolutionize enterprise computing by making data centers run 10 times faster at one-tenth the cost, leveraging its strong position in AI architectures. The company plans to disrupt Intel's x86 dominance through Arm-based architectures, integrated chip designs, and a compelling software consumption model. The article highlights Nvidia's strategic moves, financial standing, and the potential impact of its proposed acquisition of Arm Ltd. on the data center market.

title: Rain pelts down in Taiwan to provide drought relief
summary: Taiwan is experiencing significant rainfall with "extremely heavy rain" advisories issued for central counties and "heavy rain" advisories for other regions. This rain provides some relief for the country's severe drought, with chip manufacturers like TSMC and UMC anticipating water restrictions to potentially be mitigated. Meteorologists predict continued strong fronts and thunderstorms through early next week before rainfall intensity may decrease.

title: NVIDIA AI Enterprise Software Drives New Wave of Certified Systems from World’s Leading Manufacturers
summary: NVIDIA announced a significant expansion of its NVIDIA-Certified Systems program, featuring dozens of new servers from leading manufacturers that are certified to run NVIDIA AI Enterprise software. These systems, including high-volume x86 servers, are designed to bring the power of AI to various industries by supporting demanding workloads in traditional data centers and hybrid clouds. The expansion also includes new servers equipped with BlueField-2 DPUs for enhanced security and upcoming Arm CPU servers for high-performance AI computing.

title: NVIDIA Base Command Platform Provides Enterprises with Fast Path to Scale Production AI
summary: NVIDIA announced the Base Command Platform, a cloud-hosted development hub designed to help enterprises streamline AI projects from prototype to production. This platform, available through a monthly subscription with NetApp, offers access to NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD AI supercomputers and NetApp data management. Google Cloud plans to integrate the platform into its marketplace, promoting a hybrid AI experience.

title: It’s Time for Ti: NVIDIA Introduces Gaming Flagship — the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti
summary: NVIDIA has announced two new additions to its GeForce RTX family: the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti and GeForce RTX 3070 Ti. The RTX 3080 Ti, launching June 3rd at $1,199, is touted as the new flagship gaming GPU, offering 1.5x faster performance than previous generations and catering to demanding modern games and creative applications. The RTX 3070 Ti, available next week starting at $599, also delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessors.

title: NVIDIA Partners Unveil New Servers Featuring NVIDIA BlueField DPUs
summary: Several top server manufacturers, including ASUS, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, QCT, and Supermicro, announced new systems at COMPUTEX 2021 featuring NVIDIA BlueField-2 Data Processing Units (DPUs). These DPUs enhance server performance, security, and manageability by offloading networking, storage, and cybersecurity tasks from the CPU, making more resources available for applications. The servers are designed for various enterprise applications and can be easily programmed using the NVIDIA DOCA SDK, with DPU-accelerated servers expected to be available later this year.

title: AMD shows how FidelityFX Super Resolution beats out NVIDIA's DLSS
summary: AMD announced FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) at Computex 2021, an image upscaling technology designed to boost frame rates and resolution. FSR directly competes with NVIDIA's DLSS but offers broader compatibility, supporting a wide range of AMD GPUs and even some NVIDIA GeForce cards. The technology, which provides up to a 2.5 times increase in performance mode, is expected to launch on June 22, 2021.

title: NVIDIA Announces Upcoming Events for Financial Community
summary: NVIDIA announced its participation in several upcoming financial community events in June 2021, including the Evercore ISI Inaugural TMT Conference, BofA 2021 Global Technology Conference, and Nasdaq 44th Investor Conference. Interested parties can access live audio webcasts of these presentations and replays on NVIDIA's investor relations website. The company also reiterated its role in pioneering accelerated computing and AI, highlighting its impact on various industries.

title: TSMC Throws The Ball In Intel’s Court By Showcasing Customized Chipmaking Technologies
summary: TSMC announced new customized semiconductor nodes, N5A for automotive and N6RF for communications, at its online technology symposium. This move aims to solidify TSMC's position as a contract chip manufacturer by offering specialized processes, directly challenging Intel's plans to enter the contract manufacturing space. TSMC emphasized its commitment to not competing with its customers, differentiating itself from other potential foundries.

title: How to View Your Fusion 360 Designs in AR with USDz File Format
summary: Fusion 360 has introduced support for the USDz file format, enabling users to view their 3D designs in augmented reality (AR) directly from iOS mobile devices. This feature allows designers to preview designs in real-life environments, assess scale and aesthetics, and communicate concepts more effectively to clients and stakeholders. The article explains what USDz is, how to export files from Fusion 360, and highlights the benefits of using AR for design visualization.

title: Here to stay: Implications and opportunities from Taiwan’s semiconductor edge
summary: Taiwan's semiconductor industry dominance stems from decades of government policy and private sector innovation, creating a thriving ecosystem. This leadership is sustained by aggressive R&D investments and high barriers to entry, making it difficult for new competitors to catch up. Structural demand drivers like 5G, AI, and EVs are expected to fuel continued growth in semiconductor sales, presenting attractive opportunities for active investors within Taiwan's broader semiconductor ecosystem.

title: People camped out at Bakersfield Best Buy for upcoming graphics card
summary: Nearly one hundred people camped out at the Bakersfield Best Buy on Rosedale Highway for NVIDIA’s latest graphics card, the GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Founders Edition. The card was set to be released on Thursday at select Best Buy stores nationwide, with customers lining up due to global chip shortages and high demand. Employees planned to hand out tickets at 7:30 a.m., guaranteeing purchase at 9 a.m. for those who received one.

title: Super Micro Computer To Double Their Manufacturing Capacity To Meet Worldwide Server And Storage Demands
summary: Super Micro Computer, Inc. is doubling its manufacturing capacity at its US and Taiwan campuses to meet the growing global demand for servers and storage driven by Cloud, AI, and 5G/Edge technologies. This expansion aims to increase production to over two million servers per year by mid-2021 and enable the company to ship fully tested racks directly to customers. Supermicro will offer a range of application-optimized systems, including those supporting the latest Intel and AMD processors, NVIDIA GPUs, and liquid cooling options, to accommodate various workloads.

title: AMD extends FidelityFX Super Resolution to RX 470 and RX 480
summary: AMD is extending its FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) technology to older graphics cards, specifically the Radeon RX 470 and RX 480 GPUs, dating back to 2016. This digital upscaling technology is designed to improve game performance and visuals without requiring significant processing power, and it will also work with a wide range of other AMD and some NVIDIA GeForce cards. FSR is expected to launch on June 22, 2021, offering performance boosts for both high-end and older hardware.

title: Marvell Extends PAM4 DSP Cloud Data Center Leadership with Industry's First Integrated Solution
summary: Marvell has announced its Atlas 50Gbps PAM4 DSP chipset solution, which integrates transimpedance amplifiers and laser drivers into a single mainstream CMOS technology solution. This advancement significantly reduces power consumption by 25% and simplifies the supply chain for high-performance cloud data centers, computing, and AI applications. The Atlas DSP platform is designed for high-volume markets, offering cost-effective, highly integrated, and reliable technology essential for massive data center growth.

title: Tilling AI: Startup Digs into Autonomous Electric Tractors for Organics
summary: Ztractor, founded by Bakur Kvezereli, is an autonomous electric tractor startup utilizing NVIDIA's Jetson edge AI platform to address labor shortages, pesticide issues, and energy costs in organic farming. The company offers tractors equipped with numerous sensors and cameras that collect data to improve crop conditions, increase yields, and enhance efficiency, positioning the agricultural machine industry for an "electric revolution" similar to the automotive sector. Ztractor's technology, which enables tasks like precision weeding and soil preparation, aims to make organic farming more competitive and sustainable.

title: New Cadence Allegro X Design Platform Revolutionizes System Design
summary: Cadence Design Systems introduces the Allegro X Design Platform, an integrated engineering solution for system design that unifies schematic, layout, analysis, collaboration, and data management. This new platform, built on Allegro and OrCAD technology, aims to significantly streamline the design process for engineers, offering up to 4X productivity improvements through enhanced integration, cloud capabilities, and ML-driven advancements. It supports complex multi-domain designs (EM, thermal, SI/PI) and leverages GPU technology for accelerated performance.

title: Opinion: AMD’s stock has been left behind, but not for long — here’s why
summary: The article argues that Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock is a good buy despite its significant past gains, as it hasn't fully rebounded from a recent dip unlike other semiconductor stocks like Nvidia. The author attributes this potential for future growth to AMD's new cutting-edge products and a key acquisition.

title: NVIDIA to Acquire DeepMap, Enhancing Mapping Solutions for the AV Industry
summary: NVIDIA has acquired DeepMap, a startup focused on creating high-definition maps for autonomous vehicles, to enhance its mapping products and accelerate full self-driving expertise. DeepMap's technology provides centimeter-level precision mapping and continuous updates, crucial for autonomous vehicles to navigate safely and accurately. This acquisition strengthens NVIDIA's DRIVE platform by improving localization capabilities for AVs.

title: Report: Intel has offered $2B+ to acquire chip startup SiFive
summary: Intel Corp. has reportedly offered over $2 billion to acquire SiFive Inc., a chip startup specializing in processor technology based on the open-source RISC-V instruction set architecture. This potential acquisition would be one of Intel's largest recent deals, following its 2019 purchase of Habana Labs. The move could position Intel to address future demand for open-source chip designs, especially given concerns surrounding Nvidia's acquisition of Arm.

title: Invest in ETFs
summary: VanEck offers a variety of ETFs covering timeless themes like global equity, gold miners, and real estate, as well as smart themes such as semiconductors, video gaming, esports, and hydrogen. Each ETF is designed to support different investment goals but comes with specific risks that investors should carefully assess against their individual objectives. The article emphasizes conducting due diligence by referring to relevant documentation like the prospectus and Key Information Document (KID) before investing.

title: Rumor: Intel May Buy RISC-V CPU Designer SiFive to Fend off ARM
summary: A rumor suggests Intel is considering purchasing RISC-V CPU design company SiFive for $2.1 billion. This acquisition could provide Intel with a significant stake in the expanding RISC-V market, complementing its foundry efforts and potentially positioning RISC-V alongside x86 in specific market segments. The move is also seen as a strategic response to Nvidia's potential acquisition of ARM, allowing Intel to hedge its bets in the evolving CPU landscape, though SiFive's open-source nature means other companies could still develop RISC-V CPUs.

title: Nvidia acquires DeepMap as it builds out its end-to-end autonomous driving stack
summary: Nvidia has announced its acquisition of DeepMap Inc., a startup specializing in mapping technology for autonomous vehicles. This acquisition aims to enhance Nvidia's comprehensive suite of solutions for the autonomous driving sector, which already includes chips, software tools, and simulation platforms. The integration of DeepMap's technology will allow Nvidia to strengthen its competitive position against rivals like Intel's Mobileye unit by improving its mapping capabilities for self-driving cars.

title: New Semiconductor ETF Follows Famous SOX Index
summary: The Invesco PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXQ) has launched, tracking the PHLX SOX Semiconductor Sector Index (SOX), which comprises 30 components integral to disruptive technologies like NVIDIA and Qualcomm. Despite a global semiconductor shortage, the SOX index has outperformed the Nasdaq-100 and S&P 500 this year, showcasing strong growth in revenue and net income for its large-cap constituents. This new ETF offers investors exposure to the long-term growth potential of the semiconductor industry, driven by demand from everyday consumer items and advanced technologies like AI and cloud computing.

title: Trash to Cash: Recyclers Tap Startup with World’s Largest Recycling Network to Freshen Up Business Prospects
summary: AMP Robotics, founded by Matanya Horowitz, uses AI powered by NVIDIA GPUs to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recycling. The startup addresses the challenge of contaminated recyclables and the high costs associated with manual sorting by deploying robotic arms that utilize computer vision to identify and sort various materials with high precision. This technology helps recyclers increase purity, reduce operational costs, and generate more revenue from sorted materials.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Is the World’s Most Important Chip Maker. How to Play the Stock.
summary: The article highlights Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) as the world's most critical chipmaker, responsible for approximately 60% of outsourced chip manufacturing and 90% of the industry's profits. It notes that the ongoing semiconductor shortage has emphasized the importance of chips across various sectors, from simple components to high-end processors. The article then addresses how investors can approach this significant stock.

title: Bernstein recommends Sea, says Singapore-based internet company is a 'super app in the making'
summary: Bernstein recommends Sea Ltd., calling the Singapore-based internet company a "super app in the making" and initiating coverage with an outperform rating and a $350 price target. The investment firm believes Sea's strong execution track record ensures its dominance in various verticals, particularly highlighting the potential of its e-commerce arm, Shopee, to reach breakeven by 2025. Key drivers for the stock are expected to be Shopee's expansion in Latin America and grocery in Southeast Asia, leading to increased profitability.

title: Nvidia Share Price: Why Stock Split Means ‘Nothing’ to CNBC's Jim Cramer
summary: Nvidia's stock split, recently approved by shareholders, is set to make shares more accessible by reducing the price per share while increasing the number of shares held by investors. Despite a rally following the announcement, CNBC's Jim Cramer believes the split "does nothing" to increase Nvidia's appeal, arguing that investors should focus on company fundamentals rather than stock gimmicks. Analysts currently maintain a "buy" rating on Nvidia, with an average price target that suggests a slight downside from its recent trading price, though one analyst sees significant upside potential in its gaming business.

title: This is Grand Theft Auto as made by AI
summary: AI researchers have utilized Nvidia's GameGAN neural network to create "GAN Theft Auto," an entirely AI-generated version of Grand Theft Auto V. The playable demo showcases an AI-generated highway scene that, despite being pixelated, demonstrates impressive details like shadows and reflections, all without human-coded graphics. This project offers a glimpse into a future where entire games, or portions thereof, could be concocted by AI.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Acquires AI Company Determined AI to Focus on Accelerating Machine Learning
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has acquired AI startup Determined AI to accelerate machine learning models. Determined AI, founded by UC Berkeley researchers, specializes in open-source machine learning platforms that significantly reduce computation time for AI model training. This acquisition aims to combine HPE's high-performance computing with Determined AI's technology to simplify AI development and shorten time to market.

title: Longtime Intel exec Navin Shenoy leaves as chipmaker restructures data center business
summary: Longtime Intel executive Navin Shenoy is departing the company as CEO Pat Gelsinger implements a major restructuring of its critical data center business, creating two new units. The Data Platform Group is being split into a Datacenter and AI group led by Sandra Rivera, and a Network and Edge Group led by Nick McKeown. Additionally, Intel is forming a Software and Advanced Technology Group and an Accelerated Computing Systems and Graphics Group, led by Greg Lavender and Raja Koduri respectively, to better compete with rivals like Nvidia, Arm Ltd., Qualcomm Corp., and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

title: Intel Restructuring: Navin Shenoy Out; New Software, GPU Units
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has announced a major restructuring of the company, leading to the departure of top data center executive Navin Shenoy. The Data Platform Group is being split into two new business units, and two new divisions, the Software and Advanced Technology Group and the Accelerated Computing Systems and Graphics Group, are being formed. These changes aim to accelerate Intel's pace in regaining technology leadership, with new leaders appointed to head the reorganized groups.

title: Unity acquires Pixyz Software
summary: Unity Technologies has acquired France-based Pixyz Software, a specialist in 3D data optimization, for an undisclosed sum. Pixyz's technology, which helps developers import and edit 3D models in real-time, will be integrated into Unity's Create segment, but will continue to charge a separate subscription. This acquisition is part of Unity's strategy to expand its business through targeted takeovers, enhancing its offerings for both gaming and industrial customers.

title: GlobalFoundries to open new fab in Singapore
summary: GlobalFoundries is investing $4 billion to build a new semiconductor fabrication plant in Singapore, aiming to expand its manufacturing capacity amidst a global chip shortage. The facility, expected to roll out its first production wafers in Q1 2023, will create 1,000 high-value jobs and strengthen Singapore's position in advanced manufacturing. This expansion is designed to meet surging demand driven by 5G, IoT, and cloud computing.

title: 3D interactive tour of ONTAP AI
summary: NetApp offers a 3D interactive tour of its ONTAP AI proven architecture, which combines NVIDIA DGX systems with NetApp cloud-connected all-flash storage to accelerate AI workloads. The tour allows users to explore various configurations, including NVIDIA DGX A100 servers and NetApp AFF A400 and A800 storage systems, with detailed views of individual components. This solution is designed to streamline data flow and speed up analytics, training, and inference across a data fabric from edge to core to cloud.

title: NVIDIA Fleet Command Scales Edge AI Services for Enterprises
summary: NVIDIA has launched its Fleet Command managed edge AI services platform, designed to simplify the deployment and management of AI applications across thousands of locations for enterprises. This SaaS platform helps businesses securely roll out and manage AI applications on NVIDIA-Certified Systems, reducing IT burden and accelerating the adoption of AI in various industries. Early adopters include leading companies in retail, healthcare, and logistics, using Fleet Command to improve operational efficiency and address complex challenges in edge AI deployment.

title: NVIDIA Announces Instant AI Infrastructure for Enterprises
summary: NVIDIA has launched AI LaunchPad, a program that provides enterprises with immediate access to NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and software to streamline the entire AI lifecycle. Digital infrastructure leader Equinix is the first partner, offering NVIDIA-powered hybrid-cloud solutions globally that deploy in minutes. This initiative aims to simplify AI deployment for businesses by providing a comprehensive, ready-to-use hybrid-cloud platform.

title: Tesla Unveils Top AV Training Supercomputer Powered by NVIDIA A100 GPUs
summary: Tesla has unveiled its in-house supercomputer, powered by 5,760 NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, to train deep neural networks for its Autopilot and self-driving capabilities. This system achieves an industry-leading 1.8 exaflops of performance, making it one of the top five supercomputers globally. The supercomputer is crucial for processing massive datasets from Tesla's fleet of over a million vehicles, allowing for continuous iteration and refinement of their autonomous driving AI.

title: HPE should add bank card swipe to on-prem cloud for growth, says analyst
summary: A disruptive technology analyst suggests that HPE's on-premises cloud solutions, like GreenLake, should incorporate credit card payment options to offer developers greater flexibility and agility, mimicking public cloud advantages.
