This would enable easy scaling of workloads and position HPE to capitalize on the shift of data and compute to the edge. The article emphasizes the importance of edge computing, detailing the challenges and opportunities for on-prem vendors, and also touches on the future of the semiconductor industry with increased competition.

title: Nvidia’s Vid2Vid Cameo AI brings 2D photos to life in video calls
summary: Nvidia has introduced Vid2Vid Cameo, a deep learning model that enables users to display a chosen 2D image or avatar during video calls, animated by their real-time movements and facial expressions. This AI technology, soon available in the Nvidia Maxine SDK, aims to enhance professionalism, reduce bandwidth consumption, and minimize video call jitter and lag. It works by mapping 20 key facial points from a live video feed to a reference image, then synthesizing a new video stream on the receiver's end, requiring significantly less bandwidth than traditional video.

title: Volvo plans to add lidar as standard equipment in electric XC90 SUV next year
summary: Volvo Cars announced plans to make lidar sensors standard equipment in its electric XC90 SUV starting next year, a strategic move to enhance safety and autonomous driving. This decision positions Volvo differently from rivals like Tesla, which rely solely on cameras. Luminar Technologies Inc. will supply the Iris lidar and Sentinel software for this integration.

title: Nvidia’s takeover of Arm gets support from Broadcom and other chip heavyweights
summary: Broadcom, MediaTek, and Marvell have publicly expressed their support for Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm, despite scrutiny from antitrust regulators and concerns from rivals like Qualcomm, Google, and Microsoft. These chip heavyweights cite assurances from Nvidia regarding increased investment in Arm's technology and continued fair access for the industry. The support comes as Nvidia and Arm CEOs argue the deal is necessary to meet growing demand and accelerate technological roadmaps in the semiconductor industry amidst a global chip shortage.

title: Boost performance with NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage
summary: This article discusses how NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage (MIO GDS) can significantly boost performance for AI and data-intensive workloads by enabling direct data transfers between GPU memory and storage, bypassing the CPU. It highlights NetApp's AI solutions for NVIDIA DGX A100 systems, explaining how NetApp AFF and EF-Series arrays with BeeGFS integrate to leverage GDS for improved bandwidth and lower latency. The author, Mike McNamara, emphasizes the benefits for various industries and NetApp's role as a key NVIDIA partner in delivering these high-performance storage solutions.

title: NVIDIA and Global Partners Launch New HGX A100 Systems to Accelerate Industrial AI and HPC
summary: NVIDIA has enhanced its HGX AI supercomputing platform with new technologies designed to accelerate industrial AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC). The updates include the NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe GPU, NVIDIA NDR 400G InfiniBand networking, and NVIDIA Magnum IO GPUDirect Storage software, aiming to deliver extreme performance for innovation. Partners like Atos, Dell Technologies, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise are integrating these advancements into their next-generation systems, leveraging the platform to address complex challenges in various industries.

title: Nvidia integrates Arm processors with its 5G edge infrastructure platform
summary: Nvidia has announced the integration of Arm processors into its Nvidia Aerial A100 AI-on-5G platform, expanding its capabilities for 5G applications at the network edge. This move provides more choice for users, as the platform previously supported only x86-based CPUs from Intel. Additionally, Nvidia is partnering with Google LLC to establish an AI-on-5G Innovation Lab, aiming to accelerate the adoption and development of solutions on this combined AI and 5G platform.

title: Graphcore brings new competition to Nvidia in latest MLPerf AI benchmarks
summary: Graphcore, a UK-based startup, has demonstrated competitive performance against industry giants Nvidia and Google in the latest MLPerf AI benchmarks. While not securing the top spot in any test, Graphcore's results are significant when considering the fewer chips used and its commercial availability, positioning it as a viable alternative in the AI training market. Despite Nvidia's claims of "cherry-picking" comparisons and maintaining a strong overall lead, Graphcore emphasizes the economic advantage and scalability of its IPU systems.

title: Texas Instruments to buy semiconductor factory in $900 million deal
summary: Texas Instruments announced it will acquire Micron Technology Inc.'s semiconductor factory in Lehi, Utah, for $900 million in cash. This acquisition will be TI's fourth 300-millimeter wafer facility, strengthening its manufacturing capabilities and supply chain control amid a global chip shortage. The company expects the plant to begin generating revenue in the first quarter of 2023, following an investment of approximately $75 million per quarter in 2022.

title: Advisor Ross Gerber Launches Active 'Roaring '20s' ETF
summary: Advisor Ross Gerber, president and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management, has launched an actively managed ETF called the AdvisorShares Gerber Kawasaki ETF (GK). This new ETF will focus on nine investment themes Gerber believes will thrive in the post-COVID economy, offering investors access to his stock-picking expertise in a tax-efficient structure. Gerber emphasizes that the ETF is designed as a core growth fund for long-term investors, not a "get-rich-quick" scheme, and aims to provide a smoother ride than more volatile single-theme funds.

title: Focus: Qualcomm's new CEO eyes dominance in the laptop markets
summary: Qualcomm's new CEO, Cristiano Amon, plans to challenge Apple's dominance in the laptop market by developing energy-efficient chips with the help of former Apple chip architects. The company is also focusing on revenue growth from China for its smartphone chip business despite political tensions and aims to leverage its Nuvia acquisition to push 5G connectivity into laptops, providing custom-designed chips to compete with Apple. Amon also faces the challenge of potentially losing Apple as a modem chip customer and improving Qualcomm's brand recognition among consumers.

title: NVIDIA Launches UK’s Most Powerful Supercomputer, for Research in AI and Healthcare
summary: NVIDIA has launched Cambridge-1, the UK's most powerful supercomputer, to accelerate AI and simulation research in digital biology and healthcare. This $100 million investment will support projects with key partners like AstraZeneca and GSK to advance drug discovery, understand brain diseases, and improve genomic accuracy. The supercomputer is a NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD cluster, powered by 100% renewable energy, and aims to generate £600 million in economic value over the next decade.

title: NVIDIA debuts supercomputer for healthcare and AI research
summary: NVIDIA has launched the Cambridge-1, acclaimed as the UK's most powerful supercomputer, with a $100 million investment aimed at healthcare applications. The supercomputer will utilize AI to advance drug development, explore dementia causes, and identify genomic disease risk factors. AstraZeneca and GSK are among the early users, leveraging its capabilities for chemical structure modeling, digital pathology, and genetic validation of drug targets.

title: Intel Corporation names Shlomit Weiss as co-General Manager of its Design Engineering Group
summary: Shlomit Weiss is returning to Intel as Senior Vice President and co-General Manager of its Design Engineering Group, where she will oversee chip development for client computers. Weiss, who previously spent 28 years at Intel and most recently served as Senior VP for Silicon Engineering at Nvidia, will work from Israel alongside Sunil Shenoy. She brings extensive experience, having been recognized for developing Intel's Dual-Core processor architecture and leading the Sky Lake processor development.

title: Nvidia launches $100M Cambridge-1 supercomputer to support healthcare research
summary: Nvidia has launched Cambridge-1, a $100 million supercomputer in the U.K. dedicated to life sciences research. It is the fastest supercomputer in the U.K., offering eight petaflops with Linpack and 400 petaflops for AI workloads, powered entirely by renewable energy. The system will support various research projects with partners like AstraZeneca, GSK, King's College London, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, and Oxford Nanopore Technologies, focusing on drug discovery, disease understanding, and algorithm improvement.

title: Qualcomm and InterDigital among founders of new US 6G initiative
summary: A new 6G initiative named 6G@UT has been launched in the US, based at the University of Texas in Austin, with key founders including Qualcomm, InterDigital, AT&T, Nvidia, and Samsung. This initiative aims to advance 6G research with a strong focus on embedding machine learning and sensing technologies, anticipating a future where AI/ML will fundamentally transform wireless communications. The founding members emphasize the importance of collaborative research to develop intelligent networks capable of providing advanced services and supporting futuristic applications like holographic calls and immersive AR/VR.

title: Ash Bhalgat Author Page
summary: This page introduces Ash Bhalgat, Senior Director of AI Networking and Security Solutions at NVIDIA, detailing his 25 years of high-tech experience at companies like Cisco and Polycom. It highlights his expertise in various technologies, including data centers, AI, and cybersecurity. The page also features articles he's associated with, such as collaborations between NVIDIA and F5, and NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks, to enhance AI efficiency and cyber defenses.

title: Nvidia reveals how its BlueField DPUs boost Palo Alto Networks' virtual firewall performance
summary: Palo Alto Networks and Nvidia detailed their collaboration on a massively accelerated virtual next-generation firewall (NGFW) that uses Nvidia's BlueField-2 Data Processing Units (DPUs) to offload network traffic inspection from server CPUs, significantly boosting performance. The VM-Series NGFW can achieve 100 gigabytes per second throughput, a five-times improvement over CPU-only firewalls, by utilizing the DPUs for intelligent traffic filtering and offloading uninspectable or unnecessary traffic. This approach allows server CPUs to focus on compute tasks and optimizes firewall efficiency without compromising security.

title: AutoX Unveils Full Self-Driving System Powered by NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: AutoX has launched its "Gen5" self-driving system, designed specifically for robotaxis and powered by NVIDIA DRIVE automotive-grade GPUs, achieving up to 2,200 TOPS of AI compute performance. This system enables full self-driving mobility services without a safety driver, as demonstrated in Shenzhen, China, and is central to AutoX's plans for a global robotaxi rollout. The Gen5 system utilizes 28 cameras, six lidar sensors, and 4D radar to navigate complex urban environments, with NVIDIA Ampere architecture GPUs providing the necessary processing power for advanced AI.

title: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks Boost Cyber Defenses with DPU Acceleration
summary: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks have partnered to enhance cybersecurity by accelerating Palo Alto Networks' virtual next-generation firewall (NGFW) with NVIDIA's BlueField data processing unit (DPU). This collaboration significantly boosts firewall performance by offloading packet filtering and forwarding, achieving a 5x performance increase and enabling intelligent traffic offload. The new solution allows for comprehensive security coverage across all servers without compromising network speed, addressing the rising costs and sophistication of cybercrime.

title: Is Nvidia Stock A Buy Now Before Its Stock Split? (NASDAQ:NVDA)
summary: NVIDIA has announced a stock split effective July 20, which historically can lead to short-term price movements. While growth and valuation are long-term drivers, NVIDIA is well-positioned for future growth but its shares are currently historically expensive. The article explores whether NVIDIA is a buy before its upcoming stock split, considering both its growth prospects and current valuation.

title: PTC Collaborates with NVIDIA and NetApp to Launch AI Integration Hub
summary: PTC System (S) Pte Ltd has launched an AI Integration Hub in collaboration with NVIDIA and NetApp to help enterprises leverage AI and data science. The hub is built on NetApp ONTAP AI, combining NVIDIA DGX systems and NetApp All Flash FAS, and aims to accelerate the deployment of AI applications by offering free testing services. This initiative, supported by key executives from PTC, NetApp, and NVIDIA, seeks to boost AI adoption across the Asia-Pacific region, including Singapore, by providing high-performance computing infrastructure and simplified AI deployment paths.

title: Intel exploring deal to buy US chipmaker GlobalFoundries for $30B
summary: Intel Corp. is reportedly in talks to acquire chipmaker GlobalFoundries Inc. for up to $30 billion, which would be Intel's largest acquisition to date. The potential deal aligns with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger's strategy to bolster the company's chip production capabilities and compete with industry leaders like TSMC. Analysts note the acquisition could offer immediate benefits to Intel by providing access to more fabs, while GlobalFoundries' owners would secure a significant payday without the uncertainty of an IPO.

title: Intel is in talks to buy GlobalFoundries for about $30 billion
summary: Intel is reportedly in discussions to acquire GlobalFoundries for approximately $30 billion, a move that would significantly boost Intel's strategy to become a major contract chip manufacturer. This potential acquisition aligns with Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger's push to expand chip-making capabilities for other companies, a market currently dominated by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The deal, if it materializes, would be Intel's largest acquisition ever, although GlobalFoundries is also considering an initial public offering.

title: AEye’s LiDAR to be Available on The NVIDIA DRIVE Autonomous Vehicle Platform
summary: AEye, Inc. announced its adaptive, intelligent LiDAR solutions will be available on the NVIDIA DRIVE autonomous vehicle platform. This collaboration will provide ADAS and AV developers with advanced tools to enhance data quality for Level 2+ to Level 5 autonomous driving applications. Both companies emphasize that intelligence and AI-driven sensing are crucial for developing safer and high-performing autonomous systems.

title: Best Buy Is Selling Nvidia RTX 30 Series GPUs At MSRP Tomorrow
summary: Best Buy stores nationwide will be selling Nvidia RTX 30 series graphics cards at their original MSRP starting tomorrow, July 20th. Due to severe shortages and price inflation, this offers a rare opportunity for customers to purchase these GPUs at normal prices. Best Buy will be implementing a ticketing system at participating stores to manage demand and discourage scalping.

title: Nvidia Stock’s Surge Makes Chip Maker 10th-Biggest U.S. Listed Company
summary: Nvidia Corp. has become the 10th-largest U.S. public company due to a surge in its stock, driven by the post-pandemic boom in the semiconductor business. The company's shares have increased by nearly 80% over the past year, resulting in a market value of approximately $453 billion. This valuation exceeds the combined market capitalization of its rivals Intel Corp. and Broadcom Inc.

title: Newcomer Viridi Funds Launches Clean Energy Crypto Mining ETF, 'RIGZ'
summary: Viridi Funds has launched its first ETF, the Viridi Cleaner Energy Crypto-Mining & Semiconductor ETF (RIGZ), offering investors exposure to environmentally sustainable cryptocurrency. The actively managed fund will invest in companies across the crypto mining industry and infrastructure, including semiconductor producers, mining rig manufacturers, and crypto mining companies. RIGZ aims to align purpose and profit by focusing on sustainable practices within the growing crypto ecosystem, particularly in North America where over 50% of Bitcoin mining uses renewable energy sources.

title: Chip design giant Cadence launches AI platform to speed processor development
summary: Cadence Design Systems Inc. has launched Cerebrus Intelligent Chip Explorer, an AI platform designed to accelerate processor development and enhance the productivity of semiconductor engineers. The platform utilizes machine learning, specifically reinforcement learning, to automate and optimize various stages of chip design, including register-transfer level development and floorplan creation. Early adopters like Renesas Electronics Corp. and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd.'s foundry business have already seen significant improvements in chip performance.

title: Intel CEO Says Chip Shortage Could Stretch Into 2023
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger believes the global semiconductor shortage could extend into 2023, joining a growing consensus that supply chain disruptions will persist. The shortage is impacting various industries, leading to rising prices and production delays for goods ranging from consumer gadgets to automobiles. While some easing is expected later this year, a full return to supply-and-demand balance in the semiconductor industry could take one to two years due to the time required to build manufacturing capacity.

title: Cyberpower Hyper Liquid Ultra RTX PC
summary: This article reviews Cyberpower's high-end Hyper Liquid Ultra RTX PC, priced at £4,899. It highlights the system's powerful components, including a watercooled AMD Ryzen 9 5950X and Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 Ti, and critically assesses its build and performance. While praising the component selection generally, the review points out areas for improvement such as the motherboard choice, idle noise levels, and RGB control.

title: FTC changes course on prior approval for reattempted mergers
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has voted to rescind a 1995 policy statement, allowing them to routinely require prior approval for reattempted mergers and prior notice for mergers below the Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) threshold. This move, initiated by FTC Chairman Lina Khan and following President Biden's executive order, aims to bolster protections against unlawful mergers and acquisitions by removing the need for new, time-consuming investigations into deals previously deemed anticompetitive. While supported by a 3-2 vote, Commissioner Noah Phillips expressed concerns that ignoring market changes could hinder normal market operations.

title: As global demand for microchips surges, tech giants go all-in on Israel
summary: Amid a global surge in microchip demand and a component shortage, major tech companies like Google, Microsoft, Facebook, Intel, and Nvidia are establishing or expanding chip design operations in Israel. The country is benefiting from its strong R&D capabilities and skilled workforce in semiconductor design. This trend is attracting increased venture capital investment, despite challenges like a shortage of engineers and rising salaries.

title: Upcoming DL RecSys Summit: Develop and Optimize Deep Learning Recommender Systems
summary: NVIDIA, Facebook, and TensorFlow are hosting a summit on July 29 to discuss best practices for developing and optimizing deep learning recommender systems. The event will feature sessions covering high-performance model training, architectural optimization, and using TensorFlow Recommenders. Experts from these companies will share insights to help engineers and data scientists build effective recommender systems.

title: Intel to build Qualcomm chips, aims to catch foundry rivals by 2025
summary: Intel announced its factories will begin building chips for Qualcomm and Amazon, aiming to regain its leadership in chip manufacturing by 2025 against rivals like TSMC and Samsung. The company outlined a new roadmap with five chipmaking technologies and a revised naming scheme to reflect its competitive standing. This move signifies Intel's commitment to overcoming past delays and establishing itself as a leading foundry.

title: ANNUAL REPORT 2021 Arm: Business Strategy
summary: Arm's 2021 annual report highlights its business strategy as a leader in semiconductor technology, emphasizing its licensing model and significant investments in R&D since being acquired by SoftBank Group in 2016. The report details how these investments are leading to increasing revenue growth, particularly from 5G smartphone sales and the emerging Arm-based server chip market, despite challenges like the COVID-19 pandemic. It also touches on future growth drivers, including new markets like IoT and autonomous vehicles, and the planned sale of Arm to NVIDIA.

title: Corsair One a200 gaming PC review
summary: The Corsair One a200 is a compact gaming PC that combines an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X CPU and an Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 GPU in a small form factor, delivering excellent 4K gaming performance. Despite its size, it manages impressive thermal performance for the GPU due to a dual-liquid cooling system, although the CPU runs a bit hot. The PC is praised for its powerful components, ease of setup, and quiet operation, though its upgradeability is limited compared to larger systems.

title: OpenAI debuts new AI programming language for creating neural networks
summary: OpenAI has released Triton 1.0, a new programming language designed to simplify and accelerate the creation of high-speed machine learning algorithms, especially those running on Nvidia GPUs. Triton automates complex code optimizations previously requiring extensive CUDA experience, thereby speeding up AI projects and enabling more efficient algorithm development. It optimizes data movement between GPU memory, data distribution across SRAM circuits, and calculation distribution across CUDA cores.

title: AI on the bench: Cadence offers machine learning to smooth chip design
summary: Cadence Design Systems has released Cerebrus Intelligent Chip Explorer, a new software program that uses machine learning to automate aspects of chip design. This tool aims to enhance human productivity by an order of magnitude and improve chip quality metrics like power, performance, and area (PPA) by up to 20%. Cerebrus leverages reinforcement learning to run numerous experiments simultaneously, assisting designers in finding optimal solutions for increasingly complex chip architectures.

title: NVIDIA Advances Instant AI with North American Availability of Base Command Platform
summary: NVIDIA has announced the North American availability of its Base Command Platform, a hosted AI development hub providing instant access to NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD supercomputers. This platform, hosted by Equinix and part of the NVIDIA AI LaunchPad program, is designed for enterprises with large-scale, multi-user AI workflows, enabling them to accelerate AI projects from prototype to production. Adobe is an early adopter, exploring its potential to streamline machine learning development, and the platform is supported by partners like NetApp and Weights & Biases for integrated data management and MLOps tools.

title: U.K. Considers Blocking Nvidia Takeover of Arm Over Security
summary: The U.K. government is reportedly considering blocking Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to potential national security concerns. This move could complicate Nvidia's push to expand its presence in the semiconductor market through the deal with Japan's SoftBank Group Corp.

title: The U.K. may block Nvidia’s acquisition of Arm over security risks
summary: The U.K. government is considering blocking Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to potential national security concerns. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) delivered an assessment with worrying implications, leading the U.K. to be inclined to reject the takeover or impose strict conditions. Arm's critical role in the semiconductor industry and Nvidia's status as a direct competitor to many of Arm's customers are central to the concerns, prompting Nvidia to state its commitment to addressing any issues the U.K. government may have.

title: Zero Waste with Taste: Startup Uses AI to Drive Sustainable Fashion
summary: Heartdub, an AI startup and NVIDIA Inception member, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by using AI to create virtual garments and reduce waste. Their software digitizes textiles and simulates how clothes appear on the human body, significantly cutting down on physical samples, R&D costs, and lead times. This technology aims to help companies achieve zero-waste manufacturing and allows consumers to visualize clothing on digital avatars based on their own measurements.

title: Microchip Technology sees record sales as computer chip supply issues persist
summary: Microchip Technology (MCHP) reported record-setting sales at the beginning of its 2022 fiscal year, driven by the ongoing global demand for computer chips. CEO Ganesh Moorthy indicated that the entire semiconductor supply chain remains constrained, suggesting that chip shortages will extend into 2022. The company, based in Chandler, is experiencing strong demand amidst an industry-wide supply crunch.

title: NVIDIA maintains dominant position in 2020 market for AI processors for cloud and data center
summary: NVIDIA maintained its dominant position in the 2020 global market for AI processors used in cloud and data centers, holding an 80.6% share of global revenue. The company generated $3.2 billion in cloud and data center AI processor revenue, up from $1.8 billion in 2019, primarily due to its leadership in GPU-derived chips. Omdia predicts that alternative suppliers will gain significant market share in the coming years despite NVIDIA's current advantage.

title: Colorful Releases Special Edition iGame RTX 3070 LHR For Bilibili E-Sports Team
summary: Colorful has released a special edition iGame RTX 3070 LHR graphics card exclusively for China's Bilibili E-Sports team and market. This unique card features a 12-pin power connection and a dual-fan design similar to RTX 3080 and RTX 3090 Founders Edition cards. It offers a slight overclocking boost and a low hash rate, tailored for the e-sports segment in specified regions.

title: Qualcomm Bids Against Magna For Veoneer
summary: Qualcomm has made a $4.6 billion offer to acquire Swedish automotive technology supplier Veoneer, outbidding Magna International's previous $3.8 billion proposal. This move aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand its presence in the automotive market, particularly in ADAS and autonomous control systems, leveraging their existing collaboration with Veoneer. The acquisition would allow Qualcomm to offer a complete hardware and software stack to various automotive players, enhancing its growing automotive revenue stream.

title: Cattle-ist for the Future: Plainsight Revolutionizes Livestock Management with AI
summary: Plainsight, an NVIDIA Metropolis partner, is leveraging vision AI and NVIDIA GPUs to revolutionize livestock management. Their system improves accuracy in cattle counting and health monitoring, reducing financial losses and enhancing overall operational efficiency for companies like JBS USA. Beyond managing livestock, Plainsight is also collaborating with CattlePass to use vision AI for tracking cattle on the blockchain, creating digital assets with verifiable ownership and transparent lifecycle records.

title: All AI Do Is Win: NVIDIA Research Nabs ‘Best in Show’ With Digital Avatars at SIGGRAPH
summary: NVIDIA Research received the ‘Best in Show’ award at SIGGRAPH 2021 for their digital avatar technology, which integrates four AI models. This technology allows for the creation of lifelike virtual characters from a single photo, natural 3D facial animation, and text-to-speech conversion. The innovative tools aim to simplify the creation of digital avatars for various applications, including videoconferencing and storytelling.

title: What Is the Metaverse?
summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang defines the metaverse as Web 3.0, the "3D internet," a network of connected, persistent, virtual worlds that will extend 2D web pages into 3D spaces. The article highlights how NVIDIA Omniverse, built on Pixar's Universal Scene Description (USD), is enabling the creation and connection of these worlds, facilitating applications like digital twins for various industries, from fashion to manufacturing and climate prediction. The metaverse is envisioned to grow exponentially, requiring new computing models and serving as a platform for humans and AI to collaborate, particularly in robotics and industrial automation.

title: From Our Kitchen to Yours: NVIDIA Omniverse Changes the Way Industries Collaborate
summary: This article details how NVIDIA Omniverse revolutionized the creation of NVIDIA's GTC keynote, enabling distributed teams to collaborate on complex 3D scenes and simulations. It highlights Omniverse's use in creating photorealistic visuals, advanced physics simulations, and a "digital twin" of a BMW factory, ultimately crafting a compelling narrative for the event, including a virtual Jensen Huang. The piece emphasizes Omniverse's potential to transform industry collaboration and simulation.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will receive the chip industry's top award
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is being recognized with the Semiconductor Industry Association's prestigious Robert Noyce Award. The award acknowledges Nvidia's significant contributions across gaming, self-driving cars, and scientific computing. Huang will receive the honor at a dinner ceremony in November.

title: Nvidia earnings will be a data-center show, but don’t miss the software on the side stage
summary: Nvidia's upcoming earnings report is expected to heavily feature its data-center sales, with analysts projecting a significant increase. Despite its reputation for chip manufacturing, the article suggests that Nvidia's valuation warrants attention to its software contributions. The company's CEO previously highlighted strong demand for its data-center GPUs.

title: Rambus Innovates 8.4 Gbps HBM3-ready Memory Subsystem
summary: Rambus Inc. has announced its HBM3-ready memory interface subsystem, featuring a fully-integrated PHY and digital controller that supports data rates up to 8.4 Gbps, delivering over 1 terabyte per second of bandwidth. This solution aims to meet the demanding memory bandwidth requirements of AI/ML training and high-performance computing (HPC) applications, building on Rambus's expertise in high-speed signaling and 2.5D memory system architecture. The company also provides interposer and package reference designs to accelerate customers' product development.

title: Nvidia Q2 FY 2022 Earnings Report Preview: What to Look For
summary: This article previews Nvidia's Q2 FY 2022 earnings report, highlighting expectations for robust growth in adjusted EPS and revenue, though at a slower pace than the previous quarter. Investors will be closely watching the company's gross margin, a key indicator of profitability, which is expected to rise. The report details Nvidia's significant sales surge fueled by demand for processors and the semiconductor shortage, and its expansion into AI, machine learning, and data-center services.

title: Rambus Outs HBM3 Details: 1.075 TBps of Bandwidth, 16 Channels, 16-Hi Stacks
summary: Rambus has unveiled new details about its HBM3-ready combined PHY and memory controller, revealing specifications that promise a significant leap in memory performance. The new HBM3 standard could achieve up to 8.4 Gbps-per-pin, 1.075 TB/s of throughput, and support for 16 channels and 16-Hi memory stacks, more than doubling the capacity and bandwidth of HBM2E. These advancements are expected to radically speed up future GPUs and SoCs, with the first chips leveraging this design anticipated in late 2022 or early 2023.

title: TSMC overtakes Tencent to become Asia's most valuable company, as China crackdown takes a toll
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has surpassed Chinese tech giant Tencent to become Asia's most valuable firm, largely due to Beijing's ongoing regulatory crackdown on its domestic tech sector. While Tencent and Alibaba have seen their market capitalizations plummet, TSMC has benefited from a global semiconductor shortage and increased demand from various industries. TSMC plans to invest $100 billion over the next three years to increase production capacity.

title: Tesla unveils chip to train A.I. models inside its data centers
summary: Tesla has unveiled a custom D1 chip designed for training artificial-intelligence networks in its data centers, which is part of its Dojo supercomputer system. An employee stated it will be the fastest AI-training computer, aiming to process extensive computing work for models that recognize items from car camera feeds. Tesla also continues to offer and develop its "Full Self-Driving Capability" for vehicles, despite criticism regarding its level of autonomy and recent investigations.

title: Intel CEO Calls Chip Maker ‘Willing Buyer’ as Semiconductor Industry Consolidates
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has stated that the company is a "willing buyer" as the semiconductor industry consolidates. He plans to use mergers and acquisitions to support Intel's revival strategy. Gelsinger expects consolidation to continue in the industry and sees Intel as a key consolidator.

title: 8 Semiconductor Stocks to Watch as Google Makes Its Own Chips
summary: The article discusses eight semiconductor stocks to watch as major tech companies like Google begin developing their own chips, signaling a shift in the industry. It highlights the reasons behind this trend, such as companies better understanding their product goals, and then details specific companies in the semiconductor sector. Each company profile includes its core business, stock performance, and a "Portfolio Grader" rating.

title: Synopsys design software uses AI to make chips 26% more efficient
summary: Synopsys Inc. announced that its AI software, DSO.ai, helped a customer achieve a 26% gain in the power efficiency of a computer chip, a significant improvement usually associated with new manufacturing technology. This AI system integrates with Synopsys's chip design suite to optimize speed, power efficiency, and cost, with companies like Samsung and Renesas already utilizing it. The latest advancement allows the AI to consider the software running on a chip for further optimization.

title: Unstung Heroes: Startup’s AI-Powered Tomato Pollinator Gives Bees a Break
summary: Arugga, an Israeli startup, has developed AI-powered robots that use computer vision and air pulses to pollinate greenhouse tomatoes, mimicking bumblebees. These robots aim to replace "manufactured" bumblebees currently used in commercial greenhouses, offering improvements in yield and operational efficiency, especially in regions where bee imports are restricted. Arugga utilizes NVIDIA technology for its computer vision system and plans to expand the robots' capabilities to include pest detection and plant treatment, transforming agricultural practices.

title: Nvidia Announces GA of AI Enterprise on VMware vSphere and Standard Servers
summary: NVIDIA has announced the general availability of NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a suite of AI tools and frameworks designed to virtualize AI workloads on VMware vSphere and NVIDIA-Certified Systems. This initiative aims to make AI transformative power accessible to a broader range of enterprises by leveraging mainstream data center servers. Several system makers and Domino Data Lab are supporting this launch, with early adopters already utilizing the software in various industries like automotive, education, finance, and healthcare.

title: A massive restock of Nvidia RTX 30-series GPUs is happening at Best Buy today
summary: Best Buy stores across the US are holding a major in-store restock of Nvidia RTX 30-series graphics cards on August 26, 2021. The restock will include highly sought-after GPUs like the RTX 3080 Ti, RTX 3080, RTX 3070, RTX 3070 Ti, RTX 3060 Ti, and RTX 3090, with approximately 17,000 units available in total. Customers hoping to purchase a card should arrive early, as tickets guaranteeing a GPU will be distributed starting at 7:30 AM local time, and items are limited to one per customer.

title: NVIDIA Turbocharges Extreme-Scale AI for Argonne National Laboratory’s Polaris Supercomputer
summary: NVIDIA announced that the Polaris supercomputer at the U.S. Department of Energy’s Argonne National Laboratory will be powered by its accelerated computing platform. Equipped with 2,240 NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs, Polaris is designed to achieve nearly 1.4 exaflops of AI performance and will facilitate scientific breakthroughs in extreme-scale AI, including research in cancer treatments, clean energy, and particle physics. This supercomputer will also prepare researchers for Aurora, Argonne’s forthcoming exascale system, and be accessible to the broader scientific community.

title: Western Digital reportedly in advanced talks to merge with Kioxia
summary: Western Digital is reportedly in advanced talks to merge with Kioxia Holdings Corp in a deal valued at over $20 billion, which would significantly consolidate the flash storage industry. This potential acquisition would create a giant comparable in size to Samsung in the semiconductor market. The two companies already have a long-standing partnership, including joint ventures in 3D NAND manufacturing.

title: Synopsys' AI-Assisted EDA Tools Aim To Cut GPU Design Costs in Half
summary: Synopsys' new AI-assisted Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools promise to significantly reduce the cost and time required for chip design, particularly for GPUs. The DSO.ai platform can optimize various aspects of chip design, potentially cutting development time from 24 months to 24 weeks and reducing costs by as much as 50%. Companies like Samsung, Google, and Nvidia are already adopting this technology, which could also democratize chip development for smaller firms.

title: NVIDIA Stock Price and Forecast: Why is NVDA stock going up?
summary: NVIDIA stock continues to rise, hitting new all-time highs despite broader market nervousness ahead of the Jackson Hole symposium. A Reuters report about the US Department of Energy purchasing a supercomputer with Nvidia chips is cited as a catalyst. The article also touches on concerns from the UK's Competition and Markets Authority regarding Nvidia's proposed acquisition of ARM.

title: Field of AI: Startup Helps Farmers Reduce Chemicals and Costs
summary: Greeneye, an Israeli startup founded in 2017, is utilizing AI-driven smart sprayers to help corn and soybean farmers in the U.S. reduce their reliance on herbicides. By precisely targeting weeds, their technology can decrease herbicide use by up to 90%, mitigating costs and environmental contamination. Greeneye is supported by NVIDIA's Jetson edge AI platform and is a member of the NVIDIA Inception accelerator program.

title: Giving Virtual Dressing Rooms a Makeover with Computer Vision
summary: Revery.ai is transforming virtual dressing rooms using a deep learning model and computer vision powered by NVIDIA RTX GPUs and PyTorch. This technology processes millions of garment images weekly, allowing shoppers to virtually try on clothes from existing catalogs, capturing details like texture and shading. Revery.ai aims to digitize all garments, integrate with shoppers' wardrobes, and provide inclusive personalization options like varied body shapes and skin tones for an immersive online shopping experience.

title: The Chip Has Hit The Fan
summary: TSMC is delaying its 3-nanometer chip process until the second half of 2022 and plans to increase prices for both advanced (7nm, 5nm) and older chip processes (55nm, 40nm, 28nm, 16nm). These changes are influenced by the complexity of advanced chip manufacturing, supply chain issues exacerbated by the pandemic, and high demand. The article also discusses potential challenges from competitors like Intel and Samsung and the broader geopolitical implications of chip manufacturing dependence.

title: Musk Said to Oppose Nvidia’s Planned Takeover of Arm: Telegraph
summary: Elon Musk reportedly has concerns regarding Nvidia's proposed acquisition of semiconductor designer Arm, citing competition issues. The information comes from the Telegraph, which referenced multiple sources. This opposition highlights potential regulatory and competitive hurdles for the significant tech merger.

title: Duos Technologies Uses AI-Powered Inspection to Help Railway Operators Stay on Track
summary: Duos Technologies is using an NVIDIA GPU-accelerated AI railcar inspection system to significantly reduce the likelihood of train derailments caused by mechanical defects. The system, called rip, can inspect trains moving at full speed and detect a variety of issues, improving safety and efficiency while reducing inspection times. Duos's technology operates at the edge, processing large amounts of data daily, and the company aims to expand its reach and have its AI technology sanctioned by government regulators to revolutionize railway operations.

title: New Game Ready Driver Released
summary: NVIDIA has released a new Game Ready driver that includes support for 6 new G-SYNC Compatible gaming displays and 24 new GeForce Experience Optimal Playable Setting profiles. Gamers can download this driver through GeForce Experience to enjoy smoother, optimized gameplay and enhanced visual experiences on supported titles and monitors. The update also validates several OLED and IPS displays for G-SYNC compatibility, expanding choices for high-quality gaming setups.

title: Semiconductor ETF
summary: The VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF provides targeted exposure to the semiconductor sector, crucial for the ongoing "fourth industrial revolution" encompassing AI, 5G, and IoT. This ETF, the first of its kind in Europe, invests in pure-play semiconductor companies globally, focusing on those generating at least half their revenue from semiconductors. It highlights the high barriers to entry in the semiconductor industry, which protect profit margins for leading manufacturers.

title: Down to a Science: How Johnson & Johnson Boosts Its Business With MLOps
summary: Johnson & Johnson is actively integrating data science and Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) into its business to enhance manufacturing, clinical trial enrollment, and forecasting. The company emphasizes "decision science" to derive actionable insights from models and has established a Data Science Council and "bilingual data scientists" to bridge domain expertise with data science skills. This strategy, supported by powerful AI infrastructure from platforms like NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Domino Data Lab, has already demonstrated significant impact, such as improving forecasting accuracy in its vision care business and boosting revenue.

title: PayPal, Workday Lead New Names On IBD Breakout Stocks Index
summary: PayPal (PYPL) and Workday (WDAY) are identified as leading growth stocks on the IBD Breakout Stocks Index, both charging toward new buy points. Their inclusion also highlights the IBD Breakout Opportunities ETF (BOUT), which is also demonstrating breakout potential. JPMorgan recently downgraded PayPal, citing a slower-than-expected turnaround under its new CEO.

title: Toyota Motor cuts 2021-22 vehicle output on chip shortage, COVID-19
summary: Toyota Motor Corp has reduced its full-year production outlook for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2022, by 300,000 vehicles, from 9.30 million to 9 million, due to the global semiconductor chip shortage and increased COVID-19 cases in Southeast Asia. This reduction will result in 400,000 fewer vehicles produced in September and October, impacting automotive steel demand and leading to further closures of manufacturing lines in Japan. Toyota remains uncertain about production beyond November but notes that current demand for its vehicles is very strong.

title: Keycorp Stock Shows Rising Relative Strength Amid Surging Profit Growth
summary: Keycorp (KEY) saw its Relative Strength (RS) Rating increase to 77 due to strong earnings reports, including a 205% and 350% surge in year-over-year profit growth. Despite a fractional dip in its stock price reflecting market consolidation, the upgrade highlights the super-regional bank's positive momentum.

title: Synopsys PrimeSim Continuum Accelerates Design of Hyper-Convergent ICs
summary: Synopsys has launched PrimeSim Continuum, a unified workflow for circuit simulation technologies, to accelerate the creation and signoff of hyper-convergent designs. This solution provides 10X runtime improvements with golden signoff accuracy through next-generation SPICE and FastSPICE architectures and GPU acceleration technology. Industry leaders like Kioxia, Samsung Electronics, and NVIDIA have praised PrimeSim Continuum for its ability to handle complex designs, improve performance, and reduce verification times for memory, analog, and mixed-signal verification.

title: HPE finds second new CTO in 16 months with Fidelma Russo
summary: HPE has appointed Fidelma Russo, formerly of VMware, as its new Chief Technology Officer, marking the second CTO change in 16 months. Russo's extensive background in cloud services, software, and infrastructure is expected to drive innovation for HPE's GreenLake edge-to-cloud platform. This move signals HPE's strategic shift towards cloud-centric solutions to compete with off-premises rivals, despite strong Q3 financials attributed partly to increased hardware prices.

title: Manufacturing the Future of AI with Edge Computing | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: This article discusses how edge computing is transforming the manufacturing industry by integrating IoT sensors and AI to improve operational efficiency and productivity. It highlights the benefits of edge AI, such as ultra-low latency processing, enhanced security, and bandwidth savings, and explores various use cases including predictive maintenance, quality control, equipment effectiveness, yield optimization, factory floor optimization, supply chain analytics, and worker safety. The author emphasizes that edge computing enables real-time decision-making on the factory floor, minimizing downtime and maximizing output.

title: Jensen Huang: The 100 Most Influential People of 2021
summary: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, has been named one of TIME's 100 Most Influential People of 2021. He is recognized for his pivotal role in advancing artificial intelligence through the development of Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), which transformed computing capabilities for complex AI tasks. His technical prowess, compassionate leadership, and support for education have positioned Nvidia to continue driving technological advancements in the AI era.

title: NVIDIA to Drive “Advances for Decades to Come,” TIME Magazine Writes
summary: TIME magazine has recognized NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang as one of the most influential people of 2021, highlighting NVIDIA's significant impact on artificial intelligence. Andrew Ng's article in TIME emphasizes how Huang's strategic decision to adapt GPUs for general-purpose computing tasks laid the foundation for much of today's AI advancements. The article credits Huang's technical expertise and leadership for positioning NVIDIA to continue driving technological progress in AI for many decades.

title: Shares of this obscure chip component supplier have surged by over 1200% in the past three years
summary: Shares of Nan Ya Printed Circuit Board Corp., an obscure Taiwanese company that supplies essential Ajinomoto build-up film (ABF) substrates for chipmaking, have surged over 1200% in the past three years. This surge is due to ABF substrate becoming a critical bottleneck in the semiconductor industry, with supply expected to remain constrained until at least 2025. Major tech companies are struggling to secure enough of this component, leading to increased profits and investment for substrate manufacturers.

title: Nvidia ERISA Lawsuit Dismissed With Leave to Amend
summary: A U.S. District Court has dismissed an ERISA fiduciary breach lawsuit against Nvidia Corp. but granted the plaintiffs leave to amend and refile their complaint within 30 days. The court supported the plaintiffs' Constitutional standing but found their arguments regarding plan mismanagement, particularly concerning higher-cost share classes and the failure to consider collective investment trusts, insufficient without further detail. The dismissal came after the court agreed that the plaintiffs had failed to demonstrate imprudence in Nvidia's selection and retention of certain investment options, citing an "obvious, alternative explanation" related to revenue-sharing fees covering administrative costs.

title: AltShares Event-Driven ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:EVNT)
summary: The AltShares Event-Driven ETF (EVNT) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund launched on December 31, 2014, that invests in equity and debt securities of companies affected by corporate events. It currently trades at $11.75, up 1.8% year-to-date, with $10.89 million in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 1.31%. The fund's top institutional investor is Sonoma Allocations LLC, and its holdings include CyberArk Software, Electronic Arts, and various money market portfolios.

title: Trash Talk: Startup’s AI-Driven Detection System Primed to Take a Bite Out of Global Waste
summary: Recycleye, a London-based computer vision startup, is leveraging AI to significantly boost global recycling rates. By automating and enhancing the precision of waste material identification, their system aims to increase the capacity for recycling companies and improve overall recovery rates. The company, part of the NVIDIA Inception accelerator program, has successfully partnered with major waste management firms and energy leaders, developing tools like the WasteNet database and using NVIDIA's Deep Learning SDKs to achieve accuracy exceeding human vision in waste sorting.

title: NVIDIA Calls UK AI Strategy “Important Step,” Will Open Cambridge-1 Supercomputer to UK Healthcare Startups
summary: NVIDIA has welcomed the U.K. government's AI Strategy and announced that its Cambridge-1 supercomputer will be made accessible to U.K. healthcare startups. This initiative aims to accelerate drug discovery and the development of innovative products and services by providing startups with access to powerful computing resources and NVIDIA's Inception program. Peptone, a U.K. biotech company, is among the first to utilize Cambridge-1 for developing therapies for inflammatory diseases.

title: Furthering NVIDIA Performance Leadership with MLPerf Inference 1.1 Results
summary: NVIDIA demonstrated leading performance in the MLPerf Inference 1.1 benchmark across data center and edge categories with its A100 and A30 Tensor Core GPUs, outperforming CPU-only servers by up to 104x. This performance allows for the use of larger, more complex models in real-time applications and was significantly boosted by software optimizations in TensorRT 8 and NVIDIA Triton Inference Server. Additionally, NVIDIA made the first-ever datacenter category submissions with a GPU-accelerated Arm-based server, achieving new performance records and proving the readiness of the NVIDIA Arm software ecosystem.

title: Virtual prototyping tool for mobile, automotive and hyperscale systems
summary: Cadence Design Systems has launched Helium Studio, a virtual and hybrid prototyping platform designed to accelerate the development and verification of complex systems for mobile, automotive, and hyperscale applications. This tool allows early software bring-up and co-verification, significantly reducing design times for GPUs and 5G chips by enabling software and RTL bug fixing pre-silicon. It integrates with Cadence's existing verification engines, offering a unified debug experience and high throughput for developers.

title: Intel breaks ground on $20bn Arizona chip plants in battle with TSMC
summary: Intel has begun construction on two new chip plants in Arizona, a $20 billion investment aimed at increasing its manufacturing capacity and competing more effectively with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC). This move aligns with Washington's efforts to strengthen the domestic semiconductor industry. The new U.S. fabs are expected to become fully operational in 2024, contributing to Intel's strategy to attract customers currently served by its Taiwanese rival.

title: New Report Highlights Strength of U.S. Semiconductor Industry and Continued Challenges
summary: A new report from the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) details the strong global market share and R&D investment of the U.S. semiconductor industry, while also highlighting significant challenges like the ongoing global chip shortage and decreasing domestic manufacturing capacity. The report urges Congress and the White House to fund the CHIPS for America Act and consider an investment tax credit (FABS Act) to enhance U.S. semiconductor production and innovation. These measures are deemed crucial for maintaining America's economic competitiveness, national security, and technological leadership.

title: Kodiak Robotics Unveils Its Next-Generation Autonomous Truck with Plans to More than Double Its Self-Driving Fleet
summary: Kodiak Robotics announced its fourth-generation autonomous truck featuring Luminar's Iris LiDAR, ZF Full Range Radar, Hesai 360-degree scanning LiDARs, Cummins X15 TM Series engines, Bridgestone Americas smart-sensing tire technology, and the NVIDIA DRIVE platform. These new trucks prioritize modularity, discreet sensor integration, and enhanced reliability to enable scaled production and easier maintenance. Kodiak plans to more than double its self-driving fleet with 15 new PACCAR trucks, expanding its freight delivery business in Texas and potentially other U.S. corridors.

title: Quick on Their Fleet: Kodiak Builds Flexible, High-Performance Self-Driving Trucks on NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: Kodiak Robotics has unveiled its fourth-generation self-driving truck, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE Orin. The trucks feature a lightweight mapping strategy and a discreet, modular hardware design to achieve level 4 self-driving capabilities, focusing on flexibility and live perception rather than detailed pre-constructed maps. This approach addresses the high demand for delivery and the shortage of drivers in the trucking industry.

title: Dr. Morris Chang
summary: Dr. Morris Chang is celebrated for his profound global impact through the establishment of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). His vision for TSMC addressed the gap where semiconductor design companies lacked manufacturing capacity, leading to the creation of one of the world's most successful semiconductor firms. TSMC, under Chang's leadership, produces over 12 million semiconductor wafers annually for hundreds of clients and employs over 51,000 workers, embedding values like integrity and innovation into its core.

title: Intel’s new neuromorphic Loihi 2 chip brings tenfold performance boost
summary: Intel has launched Loihi 2, its new neuromorphic processor, which boasts a tenfold performance increase over its predecessor and is built using the pre-production Intel 4 manufacturing process leveraging extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUV). This chip, designed to mimic the human brain, features one million artificial neurons and aims to accelerate AI models with greater energy efficiency than traditional CPUs. Intel is also open-sourcing Lava, a framework to help developers build neuromorphic applications for the chip, marking a significant step towards commercialization in the AI chip market.

title: Shoot From the Stars: Startup Provides Early Detection of Wildfires From Space
summary: OroraTech, an NVIDIA Inception member and spinoff from the Technical University of Munich, is revolutionizing wildfire detection and monitoring using satellite data, ground-based cameras, and AI. The Munich-based startup aims to detect every fire within 30 minutes, significantly reducing CO2 emissions and damage. This year, OroraTech plans to launch its own AI nanosatellites equipped with NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX to provide even faster, real-time data for immediate action.

title: CORSAIR Debuts their new XENEON 32QHD165 Gaming Monitor, featuring an ultra-slim 32-inch QHD screen
summary: CORSAIR has launched its new XENEON 32QHD165 Gaming Monitor, featuring a 32-inch QHD IPS LED screen with a 165Hz refresh rate and compatibility with AMD FreeSync Premium and NVIDIA G-SYNC. The monitor is designed for gamers and creators, offering excellent color accuracy, HDR400 support, and integration with CORSAIR iCUE and Elgato Stream Deck software. It also boasts a versatile design with a unique stand featuring a 1/4" threading for mounting accessories and comprehensive connectivity options.

title: UK-based Ferroglobe eyes restart plan for silicon metal facility in Selma
summary: Ferroglobe PLC's subsidiary, Globe Metallurgical Inc. (GMI), is planning to restart its silicon metal facility in Selma, Alabama, due to favorable market conditions. The company aims to resume operation of one furnace in December and a second by March 2022, creating about 100 new local jobs. This move is part of Ferroglobe's strategic turnaround plan and has the support of Alabama state officials, who view it as a significant economic boost for the region.

title: GINN's Got the Goods of Quality Disruptive Companies
summary: The article highlights the Goldman Sachs Innovate Equity ETF (GINN) as a strong investment opportunity, particularly for those seeking exposure to high-quality, disruptive growth companies. Despite the S&P 500 Technology Index's flat performance in the third quarter, GINN focuses on larger, mature yet innovative companies with high return on equity (ROE), such as Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft. The fund's significant allocation to technology and healthcare sectors, combined with its emphasis on quality traits and R&D-focused companies, positions it well for continued upside.

title: Unlocking the Promise of 5G
summary: This article discusses the transformative potential of 5G technology, highlighting its enhanced performance compared to 4G LTE, including higher bandwidth, lower latency, and increased reliability. It details how F5 Networks and NVIDIA are collaborating to enable service providers to deploy 5G, leveraging solutions like network functions virtualization and NVIDIA's SmartNIC adapters for optimized data plane performance. The article also touches upon key market trends driving 5G adoption and the timeline for its widespread rollout.

title: Nvidia joins $100M funding round for MLOps startup Domino Data Lab
summary: Domino Data Lab, an MLOps startup, secured $100 million in funding from Great Hill Partners, Nvidia Corp., and existing investors. The company plans to deepen its partnership with Nvidia, integrating its platform with Nvidia's AI systems and seeking certification for Nvidia AI Enterprise. This investment will enable Domino Data Lab to expand its team and further develop its platform, which helps enterprises manage and deploy AI models, addressing challenges like infrastructure provisioning, software management, and talent recruitment in the competitive MLOps market.

title: Nvidia offers EU concessions over $54 billion Arm deal
summary: Nvidia has offered concessions to the EU antitrust regulator regarding its $54 billion acquisition of British chip designer Arm. The deal has raised concerns within the semiconductor industry about Arm's neutrality as a technology supplier. The EU will now seek feedback before deciding whether to approve the deal, demand more concessions, or open a formal investigation.

title: NVIDIA AI Enterprise
summary: NetApp, NVIDIA, and VMware have partnered to offer an enterprise-class AI solution, addressing the complexities of managing AI infrastructure. This collaboration leverages NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a cloud-native software suite optimized for VMware vSphere on NVIDIA-Certified Systems, and NetApp's enterprise-class storage. The integrated solution facilitates rapid deployment, management, and scaling of AI workloads in hybrid cloud environments, exemplified by NetApp's GPU-enabled Lab on Demand.

title: Oski Technology, an Expert in Formal Verification, Joins NVIDIA
summary: NVIDIA announced the acquisition of Oski Technology, a company specializing in formal verification methods. This acquisition aims to significantly increase NVIDIA's investment and commitment to formal verification strategies, which are crucial for ensuring the correctness of complex modern processors and new autonomous machine applications. Oski, known for its leading-edge work and expertise, has been a long-time partner of NVIDIA, and most of its employees will join NVIDIA, expanding NVIDIA's engineering presence in India.

title: China’s Robotaxis Hit the Road
summary: China is making significant strides in the development and deployment of robotaxis, with several leading companies actively testing and expanding their services. These companies, including AutoX, Baidu Apollo, Momenta, Pony.ai, and WeRide, are moving from trials with safety drivers to driverless operations, integrating advanced technologies like 5G-based C-V2X systems. The long-term strategy involves expanding robotaxi services and applying their underlying technology to other mobility solutions like autonomous buses and last-mile delivery.

title: Understanding the Buzz Around the BUZZ ETF
summary: The article discusses the VanEck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ), which debuted in March 2021 and capitalizes on the "meme stock" phenomenon. It examines BUZZ's methodology, noting that its longer lookback period means it doesn't solely focus on highly speculative meme stocks like GameStop and AMC. Instead, BUZZ's portfolio includes quality names like AMD, Apple, Nvidia, and Pfizer, and exhibits low single-stock risk.

title: EU to investigate Nvidia's $54 bln ARM bid after remedies fall short - sources
summary: The EU is expected to launch an extended antitrust investigation into Nvidia's $54 billion bid for British chip designer ARM. This comes after remedies offered by Nvidia last week failed to address competition concerns, marking a second setback for the company after a similar warning from Britain's antitrust agency. The European Commission is scheduled to end its preliminary review on October 27, initiating a four-month investigation.

title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. stock outperforms market on strong trading day
summary: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) rallied 3.92% on Wednesday, outperforming the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The stock closed below its 52-week high but outperformed competitors like NVIDIA Corp. and Intel Corp. Trading volume for AMD was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: Multi-Access Edge Computing: The Future of IoT & Connected Vehicles
summary: The article discusses the growing prevalence of IoT devices and the challenge of processing the vast amount of data they generate, especially in the automotive industry. It highlights how Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC), originally developed by telecommunications companies, offers a solution by processing data closer to the source, significantly reducing latency and improving reliability. MEC is presented as crucial for the future of connected vehicles, enabling new services, enhancing customer experience, and allowing for new revenue streams for OEMs.

title: MLOps startup Weights & Biases valued at $1B after fresh $135M funding round
summary: Weights & Biases Inc., an MLOps startup whose software aids in AI model development for companies like OpenAI and Nvidia, has secured $135 million in Series C funding. This investment values the company at $1 billion, bringing its total funding to date to $200 million. The platform enhances developer productivity by streamlining the organization and processing of project data and optimizing AI model configuration settings through Bayesian optimization.

title: Lenovo Extends Exclusive Lenovo Legion PC and Monitor Partnership with Apex Legends Global Series
summary: Lenovo has renewed its exclusive partnership with the Apex Legends Global Series (ALGS), providing over 400 high-performance Lenovo Legion PCs and gaming monitors for its esports competitors. This collaboration aims to power transformational gaming experiences and gather user insights from elite players to inform future product development. The partnership emphasizes Lenovo's commitment to high-performance gaming equipment and its vision in the growing esports industry.

title: Looks Can Be Perceiving: Startups Build Highly Accurate Perception Software on NVIDIA DRIVE
summary: This article highlights how startups are developing highly accurate perception software for autonomous vehicles using NVIDIA DRIVE AGX. Companies like aiMotive, Stradvision, Phantom AI, and CalmCar are leveraging the platform's high-performance, energy-efficient AI compute to enable robust object detection and safe navigation, even in challenging conditions. The platform integrates various sensor data, offering scalable solutions for both fully autonomous and AI-assisted driving systems.

title: Check out Cipher Mining Equity Warrant Exp 26th Aug 2026's stock price (CIFRW) in real time
summary: This article provides real-time stock information for Cipher Mining Equity Warrant Exp 26th Aug 2026 (CIFRW), including its current price, historical performance metrics, key financial stats, and recent news. It highlights the company's profile as an industrial-scale data center construction and operations firm focused on bitcoin mining and high-performance computing, along with insights from analyst calls.

title: Is Cyngn IPO (CYN) Stock a Good Buy?
summary: Cyngn (CYN) made its IPO debut on October 20, 2021, focusing on developing autonomous driving software for commercial industrial vehicles. While the company addresses a massive total addressable market by aiming to improve safety, increase productivity, and lower costs in industrial settings, it launched as a pre-revenue entity. This means investing in CYN stock carries significant risk despite its compelling narrative and potential to disrupt industrial sectors, requiring long-term patience from investors.

title: S&P 500 rises to record close, posts 7th straight day of gains on better-than-expected earnings
summary: The S&P 500 reached a new record close, marking its seventh consecutive day of gains, driven by strong quarterly earnings reports and year-end optimism. Despite some concerns about inflation and Fed bond tapering, corporate profits have largely exceeded expectations, with notable performances from Tesla, HP Inc., and other tech companies. The positive economic news, including a drop in jobless claims, contributed to the market's rally, though IBM's revenue miss stood out as a laggard.

title: Micron announces big changes, expansive plans. What we know about the impact on Boise
summary: Micron Technology Inc. plans to invest over $150 billion in memory-manufacturing capacity and R&D over the next decade, with potential impacts on its Boise headquarters. While Boise is the primary R&D center for DRAM and employs 5,600 people, the company remains vague about specific expansion plans in the city, pending U.S. government incentives like the Chips for America Act and the FABS Act to offset higher domestic manufacturing costs. This investment comes amid a global computing-chip shortage and aims to secure Micron's position in the semiconductor market.

title: Why Micron Needs to Build in Boise!
summary: Micron, the third-largest private employer in Idaho, announced a $150 billion global investment in memory chip manufacturing and R&D, showing interest in expanding facilities within the U.S. The article advocates for Micron to invest some of these funds locally in Boise, highlighting its historical commitment to the company and Idaho's pro-business environment. It also mentions Micron's importance as the only American-based chip manufacturer and its past expansions in Virginia and Taiwan.

title: Aruba introduces the distributed data center switch
summary: Aruba has partnered with Pensando to unveil the CX 10000, a 48-port L2/L3 Ethernet switch featuring embedded Pensando ASICs for security services, load balancing, and firewalls. This distributed data center switch allows companies to build a switching fabric across multiple locations and integrates security directly at the leaf level to enhance performance. While it pushes for a change in traditional separate management of switching and security, analysts predict a significant future market for such integrated distributed switches, especially for large enterprises.

title: NVIDIA Introduces the Next Generation in Cloud Gaming
summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation cloud gaming platform, GeForce NOW, which will offer GeForce RTX 3080-class gaming performance through a new high-performance membership tier. This tier leverages NVIDIA's SuperPOD architecture, providing significant graphical horsepower and enabling high resolutions, fast frame rates, and low latency across various devices. The service provides access to over 1,100 games, including many popular free-to-play and upcoming titles with RTX ON.

title: Diversification away from Taiwan chipmakers is necessary
summary: The article discusses the global reliance on Taiwan's chipmakers, particularly TSMC, amidst a worldwide chip shortage. It highlights efforts by South Korea, China, and the U.S. (Intel, GlobalFoundries) to diversify semiconductor production, acknowledging the difficulties due to high capital investment and technological complexity. The author concludes that while diversification is necessary, it will be a challenging and time-consuming process given Taiwan's established and highly specialized chipmaking ecosystem.

title: Nvidia Gets a Price Target Boost. Bitcoin’s Impact on Gaming May Be Ending.
summary: Piper Sandler has become more bullish on Nvidia, boosting its price target for the company. This comes amid signs that the influence of Bitcoin mining on Nvidia's gaming business might be diminishing. Nvidia is a major producer of graphics processing units (GPUs).

title: AMD Grows Revenue In Sixth Straight Quarter Reveal Q3 2021 Results
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) reported significant revenue growth for its third fiscal quarter of 2021, marking its sixth consecutive quarter of revenue increase, driven primarily by its Enterprise, Embedded and Semi-custom segment. The company recorded $4.3 billion in net sales, representing a 54% annual and 12% sequential growth, with strong contributions from data center and custom-design chips. Despite a sequential drop in cash flows due to investments in long-term supply chain capacity, AMD doubled its operating income and achieved a 78% annual net income growth, with projections for continued revenue and gross margin improvement in the current quarter.

title: Intel teams with Google Cloud to develop new class of data center chip
summary: Intel Corp and Google Cloud have collaborated to create "Mount Evans," a new class of chip called an "infrastructure processing unit" (IPU) aimed at optimizing cloud computing data centers. This chip separates and speeds up overhead tasks like setting up virtual machines, improving efficiency and security. Intel hopes to make this IPU an industry standard beyond Google, with both companies working on releasing free software tools.

title: India to push manufacturing of semiconductors
summary: India plans to boost domestic semiconductor manufacturing with significant capital and production-linked incentives. This initiative, driven by the Prime Minister's Office, aims to address the global chip shortage exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic and geopolitical tensions, which severely impacted industries like the auto sector. The government seeks to attract investors by providing financial support and tax reductions, anticipating a surge in semiconductor demand as India's electronics production rapidly grows.

title: Investing in Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of the Metaverse with an ETF
summary: This article discusses investing in Mark Zuckerberg's vision of the Metaverse following Facebook's rebranding to Meta. It explains what the Metaverse is, how investors can gain exposure through companies involved in its creation like Roblox and Unity Software, and highlights the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (NYSE:META) which tracks a basket of such stocks. The article also provides information on thematic ETFs and the fund manager, Roundhill Investments.

title: Nvidia Hits Record High as Stock Surge Nears 120% This Year
summary: Nvidia Corp. stock rallied to a record high, extending its 2021 advance to nearly 130%. The chipmaker's shares rose 12% in its sixth consecutive positive session, making it the biggest gainer in the Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index. Wells Fargo also raised its price target on Nvidia, citing opportunities in the metaverse.

title: Arista Gains Big on Cloud Boom
summary: Arista Networks experienced significant stock gains following strong earnings and boosted guidance, driven by increased capital spending from hyperscalers like Meta and Microsoft. The company also continues to gain market share from competitors like Cisco in both data center, cloud, and campus networking segments, indicating a robust cloud boom across the industry. Other infrastructure vendors like NVIDIA, Amazon Web Services, and Broadcom are also seeing growth.

title: GOI to launch a mega-billion plan for semiconductor manufacturers
summary: The Indian government is set to introduce a significant capital and production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme to boost domestic semiconductor manufacturing, addressing global chip shortages. This initiative involves discussions with major global chipmakers like TSMC and Intel, offering financial support, tariff cuts, and leveraging programs like SPECS. The move aims to capitalize on rising domestic demand, project electronic production to reach $350-400 billion by 2025, and attract investments following China's "Plus One" policy.

title: How Intel plans to catch Samsung and TSMC and regain its dominance in the chip market
summary: Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger has outlined an ambitious plan to regain dominance in the chip market by 2025, aiming to surpass competitors Samsung and TSMC. The strategy involves significant investment in new fabrication plants globally, totaling over $44 billion, and opening Intel's fabs to other companies through Intel Foundry Services. This move addresses past production missteps and aims to leverage government subsidies like the CHIPS Act to boost U.S. chip manufacturing.

title: EXPLAINED: What is Metaverse and Why Facebook/ Meta Thinks it's the Future of Internet
summary: This article explains the concept of the metaverse, why Facebook (now Meta) views it as the future of the internet, and what its potential applications are. It details how the metaverse would work, from virtual interactions and business opportunities to the technologies being developed to build it, while also touching on data privacy concerns.

title: AMD Blitzes Intel, Nvidia With New Faster EPYC, Instinct Chips
summary: AMD announced new EPYC CPUs and Instinct GPUs aimed at challenging Intel and Nvidia in data center workloads for high-performance computing and AI. The new EPYC processors (Milan-X) feature 3D chiplet technology to triple L3 cache, dramatically increasing performance, especially for technical computing. The Instinct MI200 series GPUs are positioned as "the world's fastest HPC and AI accelerator," promising up to 4.9 times faster HPC and 20 percent faster AI performance compared to Nvidia’s A100 GPU.

title: AMD lands Meta as customer and takes on Nvidia, sending shares up 11%
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares rose 11% after announcing Meta Platforms Inc. as a new data center chip customer, intensifying its competition with Intel. AMD also unveiled new chips, including the MI200 for AI and machine learning to challenge Nvidia, and the Bergamo processor for cloud computing to compete with Ampere Computing. These strategic moves bolster AMD's market position against larger rivals and secure its presence with major cloud providers.

title: Innoviz Perception Solution Supported on NVIDIA DRIVE Platform
summary: Innoviz Technologies announced that its advanced perception solution is now supported on the NVIDIA DRIVE platform, integrating its LiDAR sensor and perception software into NVIDIA's end-to-end AI platform for autonomous vehicles. This collaboration allows Innoviz's technology to enable object detection, tracking, and classification, as well as obstacle detection and calibration, and is integrated with NVIDIA DRIVE Sim for development and validation. The partnership aims to accelerate the development and deployment of autonomous vehicles by providing customer access to Innoviz's LiDAR solutions within the NVIDIA DRIVE ecosystem.

title: Supermicro Enhances Broadest Portfolio of Edge to Cloud AI Systems with Accelerated Inferencing and New Intelligent Fabric Support
summary: Supermicro announced enhancements to its AI GPU server portfolio, integrating new NVIDIA Ampere-family GPUs to deliver up to 10x faster AI inference performance and 3x faster training. These systems are designed for a wide range of applications from edge computing to cloud environments, critical for uses like autonomous driving, video streaming, and cloud gaming. Supermicro also introduced its Universal GPU Platform and systems supporting the new NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand product line, alongside optimized solutions for NVIDIA Omniverse Enterprise.

title: Nvidia picks Luminar's lidar for self-driving tech, sending its shares up 15%
summary: Luminar Technologies Inc. saw its stock jump 15% after Nvidia announced it would use Luminar's lidar technology for its self-driving platforms. This news coincided with Nvidia's annual GTC conference. Luminar has also recently partnered with Volvo and is expanding into the Chinese market.

title: NVIDIA Announces Omniverse Replicator Synthetic-Data-Generation Engine for Training AIs
summary: NVIDIA has announced Omniverse Replicator, a powerful synthetic-data-generation engine designed to produce physically simulated synthetic data for training deep neural networks. The first applications, NVIDIA DRIVE Sim and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, will accelerate the development of autonomous vehicles and robots by generating diverse and accurate datasets that cover rare or dangerous scenarios. This technology aims to augment real-world data, enabling developers to create high-quality AI models and generate ground truth data that is challenging for humans to label.

title: NVIDIA Announces Platform for Creating AI Avatars
